💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a fresh "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games.
  • "Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of newly introduced mods right now uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making.
  • Industry observers note that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the upcoming "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a fresh "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of newly introduced mods right now uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an concern related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon.".

Industry observers note that cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the upcoming "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is key for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the problem for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected.".

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the New Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

It has been revealed that personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for latest mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this update does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (703 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders.
  • Recent findings suggest that the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins.
  • Mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature.

Recent findings suggest that the findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders.

Mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model.

Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms.

The discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans.

In a recent development, worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling notable features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal.

It has been revealed that to investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity.

In a recent development, the researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation.

"We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," says Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12.".

Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder?

Industry observers note that to explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome.

These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder.

It has been revealed that although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognized. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions.

It has been revealed that "Our study is a good example of how basic research on model organisms can provide upcoming insights into human diseases," notes Adam Antebi, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing and lead author of the study. "A fundamental biological question can thus give rise to a new approach that could also become medically relevant in the long term.".

Industry observers note that materials provided by Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

  • Nearly 263,000 EVs were sold in the US in the third quarter, according to Kelley Blue Book, marking the most since the record-setting third quarter of 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Forget waiting in line for a discounted TV or other gadget you probably don’t need. If you’ve been looking to go electric, Black Friday may be the time to do it. Several brands, including Kia, Lucid, and Volkswagen, are offering $10,000 or more off select EVs right now.

While electric vehicle sales have slowed in the US after last year’s rush of buyers trying to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, the market is bouncing back.

Nearly 263,000 EVs were sold in the US in the third quarter, according to Kelley Blue Book, marking the most since the record-setting third quarter of 2025.

With upcoming models hitting the market, prices have also come down over the past year. The average transaction price (ATP) for a new EV in October was $56,221, down 2.9% from a year ago.

For Black Friday, several automakers are sweetening the deal this year, offering a generous $10,000 or more off select EVs.

Lucid launched its Black Friday offers this week. Through November 30, you can score a $15,000 Black Friday Credit on a upcoming 2027 Lucid Gravity Touring.

Prefer a sedan? Lucid is also offering a $10,000 Black Friday Credit on a fresh 2027 Lucid Air Touring. To take advantage of the offer, you must pay cash or use third-party financing.

The 2027 Lucid Gravity Touring starts at $79,900 and offers up to 337 miles of EPA-estimated range. It’s available to lease for as low as $749 a month. The offer is for a 36-month lease with $6,249 due at signing.

Lucid’s electric sedan, the 2027 Air Touring, is priced from $79,900 and offers up to 431 miles of range.

Both the Gravity and Air can add up to 200 miles of range in under 12 minutes with 400 kW DC fast charging.

Lucid’s Black Friday offers end on November 30, 2026.

Kia is offering $10,000 off several electric vehicles for Black Friday, including the three-row EV9 and the Niro EV.

According to recent reports, the 2026 Kia EV9 is available with a $10,000 Customer Cash discount that can be applied toward the purchase price. With a $10,000 discount, prices for the base EV9 Light RWD trim can fall to as low as $44,900 ($54,900 starting MSRP).

Kia is also promoting a lease deal on the 2026 EV9 Light Long Range RWD for $339/month for 36 months, with $4,999 due at signing.

If you opt to finance, you can get 0% APR for 60 months, plus $5,000 in APR Bonus Cash across the entire 2026 EV9 lineup.

The 2026 Kia Niro EV is also available with a $10,000 Customer Cash discount, knocking the price down to as low as $29,700 ($39,700 MSRP).

With leases starting at just $289/month for 36 months (with $3,999 due at signing), the 2026 Niro EV Wind FWD is about as cheap a lease as you can get nowadays, gas or electric.

The Niro EV is also available with 0% APR for up to 72 months, including a $3,500 APR Bonus Cash discount.

While it isn’t $10,000 off, it is worth mentioning that Kia now sells the smaller EV3 electric SUV. The 2027 Kia EV3 (see our review) starts at just $28,890, making it one of the most affordable EVs you can get in the US, alongside the new Chevy Bolt and Nissan LEAF.

Kia is offering a $1,500 Customer Cash discount on the 2027 EV3, which still makes it cheaper to buy outright than the Niro EV, even with incentives.

The 2027 Kia EV3 Wind FWD is available for lease starting at $349/month for 36 months, with $3,999 due at signing. Kia is offering 0.90% APR for 48 months on all 2027 EV3 trims.

Kia’s current deals end on January 04, 2027.

As it prepares to introduce its replacement in 2027, Volkswagen introduced a $10,000 Customer Bonus for the 2026 ID.4 electric SUV.

Since the ID.4 is discontinued after the 2026 model year, it might not be so easy to find one. Volkswagen remarked the remaining inventory is very limited.

If you can find one, Volkswagen will apply the $10,000 discount when you purchase or lease a new 2026 ID.4 through a participating dealer.

Volkswagen’s current ID.4 offer runs until November 30, 2026. You can read more about its replacement, the ID. Tiguan here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some mid-cycle updates focus on aesthetics, bringing some newly introduced style (and hopefully some new eyes) to a slightly older product. The 2027 Toyota Sienna skipped those pleasantries and focused on the meat and potatoes: its hybrid powertrain.

Sources indicate that the 2027 Toyota Sienna looks no different—unless you count the Cypress paint color, which was dropped and swapped with Storm Cloud—but it’s what’s lying under the body that matters more here. The Sienna adopts Toyota’s sixth-generation hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the upscale Lexus ES Hybrid. A new electric motor packs more efficient silicon-carbide conductors, and it pairs with a 1.15-kWh battery that ditches the old nickel-metal hydride chemistry in favor of lithium-ion. In addition, there’s a whole new electrical platform underpinning it all, with new ECUs and software to manage everything.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 94043.

Combine all that with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine that has been retuned for quieter low-speed operation, and you have a Toyota Sienna that produces a whopping six horsepower more than before, rising from 245 horses to 251. Engine torque is unchanged at 176 pound-feet, and Toyota did not specify e-motor torque. That small power bump is enough to affect its acceleration: Toyota estimates a 7.5-second sprint to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive Sienna variants, rising to 7.6 seconds with AWD. That’s 0.3 or 0.4 second quicker than before, respectively.

Even with that bump in speed, Toyota claims improved fuel economy in the 2027 Sienna, to the tune of +3 mpg in the city for FWD models and +4 mpg in the city for AWD models. Combined estimates rise 1 or 2 mpg. For context, the 2026 model is EPA estimated at 36 mpg city/36 highway/36 combined for the front-driver, and 35/36/35 for the AWD.

Recent findings suggest that there have also been some tweaks to other electrical-adjacent components. The electronic power steering promises less effort at low speeds, while improving on-center feel at highway speeds. That adjustment includes a new steering-wheel layout that will eventually migrate to other sixth-gen-equipped hybrids. Toyota also fiddled with its brake electronics, resulting in less pedal effort and a smoother blend between regen and friction braking. The Sienna also includes something Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels with the aim to reduce body roll during cornering.

It has been revealed that creature comforts get some upgrades as well. A 12.3-inch infotainment screen is now standard across the lineup (the LE grade ditches its 8.0-incher), as is a 12.3-inch gauge cluster (LE and XLE get this instead of the old 7.0-inch getup). There’s newly introduced LED cabin lighting, plus a revised rear-seat entertainment system that now features native apps on a new touchscreen. Upgraded dashboard sound abatement promises to lower the cabin volume by one decibel.

See all results for upcoming 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 94043.

In a recent development, toyota also slimmed down the Sienna’s trims for 2027. The Limited grade has been dropped in favor of adding more features to the sporty XSE variant, which rises to become the trim underneath the Platinum. As a result, the 2027 Sienna XSE picks up niceties like ventilated front seats with memory, a panoramic-view monitor, and a head-up display. The rugged Woodland Edition trim also picks up the surround-view tech. The upgraded rear-seat entertainment is available on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum trims.

Industry observers note that the 2027 Toyota Sienna reaches dealerships in early—you guessed it—2027. Pricing starts around $44,500 for the front-wheel-drive LE base trim, which represents a price bump of less than $2000 over a base 2026 Sienna. Not too shabby for a whole new generation of powertrain.

A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

Sources indicate that in a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the organization." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

Recent findings suggest that skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road.
  • Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.
  • According to recent reports, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s upcoming Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

According to recent reports, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment states its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

Industry observers note that “We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” mentioned Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

Moment Energy states Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

Recent findings suggest that that matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

According to recent reports, moment Energy also notes an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

Breaking: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them?
  • Recent findings suggest that the technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results.
  • Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising upcoming method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.

Recent findings suggest that the technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.

A Newly introduced Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy.

The breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.

According to recent reports, quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can quickly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.

It has been revealed that but quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," says Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties.".

In a recent development, rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the newly introduced approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify important interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.

"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy.".

Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator.

Sources indicate that to evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.

In a recent development, after this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, highlighted that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.

This represents an vital step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.

Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems.

The next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.

"This is particularly crucial because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important.".

The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.

Looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.

"After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," claims Peter Zoller.

This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how rapidly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.

The findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that automakers love to lean on nostalgia.
  • FullGood made an unexpected appearance at the Los Angeles auto show, where it is looking to find a partner to help bring its retro-themed vehicles to the United States.
  • Now FullGood wants to make a return to the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that automakers love to lean on nostalgia. Whether it’s a new paint job inspired by an old race car, or reviving a classic nameplate for a new model, utilizing a rich history can be an easy way to grab customers’ attention. But what if a company leaned on the heritage of other automakers? That’s where FullGood Motor, a Chinese company that builds modern plug-in hybrids inspired by classic cars, steps in, and FullGood now wants to break into the U.S. market.

FullGood made an unexpected appearance at the Los Angeles auto show, where it is looking to find a partner to help bring its retro-themed vehicles to the United States. The tech giant was formed back in 1995 as a motorcycle business called Loose Motor, and didn’t get into the automobile business until 2009. In fact, the pivot to cars was initially based out of a factory in California, before the company moved its operations to Beijing, China, in 2018, adopting the FullGood name in 2022.

See all results for used cars for sale near 90011.

Now FullGood wants to make a return to the United States. The organization states business is strong in China, where its factory has a 100,000-unit-per-year capacity, hence the desire to expand. We spoke with the company’s vice president, Erelly Cai, at the LA auto show to understand a bit more about the brand’s desire to come to the U.S. and the potential hurdles it might face.

The company knows it can’t enter the U.S. market alone, especially in an era where regulations make it nigh on impossible for Chinese automakers to import their vehicles. FullGood acknowledges this challenge and is in Los Angeles seeking to talk with investors and potential American manufacturing and distribution partners.

The plan is to export vehicles from China in component form, and then complete final assembly in the U.S. The vehicles would then be sold and registered under its American partners’ brand. It also wants to develop more vehicles directly inspired by midcentury American design.

FullGood brought one of its cars to the show, a seven-seat van named the Summer that is undoubtedly inspired by the Volkswagen Type 2, better known as the Microbus. Like all of its models, the Summer uses a plug-in hybrid powertrain. The Summer pairs a turbocharged 1.5-liter engine with electric motors from Wuling, a large and well-established Chinese automaker, and a 28-kWh battery from CATL. The front-wheel-drive powertrain produces a combined 325 hp, with electric-only driving range listed at 93 miles and total range at 497 miles. The Summer costs the equivalent of $49,000 at current exchange rates.

See all results for used cars for sale near 90011.

It has been revealed that cai remarked that the manufacturer would likely use the same powertrain if it manages to introduce its vehicles to the U.S. market, with the bigger obstacle being the car’s software. The U.S. Department of Commerce’s Connected Vehicle Rule bans foreign-made cars that feature certain connected software and hardware from China and Russia. Some companies that import from China, such as Volvo, have been granted an exemption, while others, like Polestar, have been banned from the U.S.

Sources indicate that fullGood hopes the LA show can help it find a partner, so “maybe we can solve the problem together,” Cai remarked. The idea would be to replace the software with a upcoming setup for the U.S. market, while keeping things like the chassis, powertrain, and interior trimmings unchanged. Along with the Summer, FullGood’s current planned lineup includes the Dolphin, which looks like a C1 Corvette; the Rocket, which emulates the 1959 Cadillac Eldorado; and the HotRod, which looks like a Ford Model A.

If FullGood manages to find a partner and bring their cars to the United States, it imagines capturing a market of buyers who are nostalgic for vehicles from their past. “They have their childhood memories,” Cai said, with FullGood’s vehicles helping to “bring those memories back.” While FullGood is still a long way from getting its cars to our shores, they certainly provide a different attitude than the current crop of vehicles sold in the U.S., with their cheery, whimsical designs, and while the barrier to getting here is high, we’re curious to see where FullGood’s Los Angeles appearance takes the oddball company.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is preparing to launch a newly introduced flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the newly introduced flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A new creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo remarked after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

The latest flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously said the company expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview highlights a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD noted earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

The Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

In a recent development, BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo stated to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Steam's newly introduced Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (448 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck.
  • According to recent reports, the thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide.
  • By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

According to recent reports, the thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

There's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that upcoming games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

As for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is at the moment only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

Japan’s three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News. The outlet reports that Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association chairman Koji Sato, who is also the vice chairman of Toyota, revealed the decision at a news conference in Tokyo this week.

In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has aims to move to more components that cover the entire car. The three areas were chosen as the first to be standardized because they are parts that are generally not noticed by consumers, and they shouldn’t have an impact on any brand’s individual identity. All three are also areas that account for significant production costs for the automakers, meaning they can have an immediate impact.

In a recent development, the first discussions of standardization are set to include Japan’s domestic automotive parts suppliers, though international suppliers will be brought into the fold in time. The first standardization efforts are set to go into place next year, according to the AN report.

Recent findings suggest that the push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan’s seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. The automakers are mentioned to hope that they can channel the money saved by homogenizing into new innovations.

“We all share this strong sense of crisis, creating a momentum for change,” Sato mentioned. “Based upon our sense of a crisis, we decided to choose these three areas.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6.
  • Industry observers note that this wasn't simply an overlooked feature.
  • In its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you can deal drugs, pay for private dances at strip clubs, and even mow down pedestrians in GTA 6. One old activity, though, isn't making the cut. Players can no longer hire sex workers, ending a feature that's been part of the series since Grand Theft Auto 3 arrived in 2001.

Industry observers note that this wasn't simply an overlooked feature. Rockstar deliberately left it out. Shacknews asked the GTA studio about it, and they confirmed the feature was removed. Rockstar also offered an explanation, and it comes down to the kind of story it wants to tell with Jason and Lucia.

In its response to Shacknews, Rockstar described GTA 6 as a story about a couple on the run. The studio mentioned it had considered which familiar GTA elements would work alongside the characters and the relationship at the center of the game, rather than bringing back every previous feature by default.

It has been revealed that rockstar pointed to systems such as police pursuits, radio stations, robberies, and car theft as examples of the elements it carried forward. Those all fit the criminal adventures Jason and Lucia get caught up in. Hiring sex workers, apparently, didn't fit what the team had in mind.

It's an interesting explanation because Rockstar didn't claim the removal was due to a technical limitation or a ratings requirement. Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

Rockstar framed the removal as a creative decision tied to Jason and Lucia's story.

It has been revealed that anyone who's watched the GTA 6 launch trailer will have seen how much of the marketing revolves around the pair. Rockstar keeps bringing the focus back to Jason and Lucia, even when the trailers show off everything else happening in Leonida. Their story is the reason the two playable protagonists are together in the first place.

Industry observers note that hiring sex workers first became a recognizable open-world interaction in GTA 3, and it remained available across later mainline games, including Vice City, San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5. For some players, it became one of those strange little things they expected to find when wandering around a GTA city at night.

Recent findings suggest that it also brings back one of GTA 3's more infamous controversies. Players could hire a sex worker, kill her afterward, and pick up the money they'd just spent. That drew plenty of criticism at the time, and the mechanic stuck around. It was still possible in GTA 5.

I can't help connecting this to Jason Schreier's 2022 Bloomberg report, which remarked Rockstar was trying to avoid jokes that punch down at marginalized groups. He suggested GTA 6 might feel quite different from GTA 5, and seeing this particular feature disappear makes me think he might have been onto something. Rockstar says it's about Jason and Lucia, of course, but I wonder if both things played a part.

Industry observers note that it was never the reason most people played these games, of course. But GTA has always made a point of filling its streets with activities that aren't strictly necessary for completing missions. The series' reputation comes as much from those distractions as it does from car chases, shootouts, and elaborate heists.

That's why removing a relatively minor interaction is still newsworthy. It has survived several generations of GTA, across different protagonists and settings. Now that Rockstar is putting two characters in a relationship at the heart of its newest game, that particular carryover has finally been dropped.

According to recent reports, this doesn't mean GTA 6 has suddenly become a tame version of Grand Theft Auto. The game's nightlife is very much present. Our guide to GTA 6's strip clubs already covers several venues around Leonida, so the absence of one activity shouldn't be confused with the removal of adult entertainment altogether.

In a recent development, there's a distinction between the atmosphere of Vice City and the specific actions Rockstar lets the protagonists take. A setting can still have strip clubs and the more outrageous side of GTA without including every interaction that existed in previous games.

The confirmation is also about a specific action players can take. It doesn't establish whether sex workers appear in the game as background characters, or whether the story mentions them. Rockstar answered a question about the gameplay interaction, not every possible appearance of the subject.

Sources indicate that some fans will probably find the change strange, particularly if they've been playing since the PS2 days. Others might not have noticed the feature was missing at all. Either way, it's one of the clearer examples of Rockstar choosing to leave an old mechanic behind instead of carrying it over simply because it's always been there.

For a series known for giving players countless ways to get distracted, that's a notable decision. And this time, at least, Rockstar has given a pretty straightforward reason for making it.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that according to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles.
  • Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

It has been revealed that according to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

According to recent reports, zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Recent findings suggest that zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

In a recent development, respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA noted in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

Breaking: Fresh wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A newly introduced wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most notable stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery.
  • Known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time.
  • REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A newly introduced wearable patch could offer a surprisingly simple way to improve one of the most notable stages of sleep, without relying on medication or surgery. Developed by researchers led by the University of Texas at Austin, the device uses gentle ultrasound waves to stimulate regions deep inside the brain, helping people enter REM sleep sooner and spend more time in this restorative stage.

Known as NEUSLeeP, the soft patch attaches to the skin and combines ultrasound stimulation with electrodes that monitor brain activity in real time. This allows researchers to influence brain regions involved in sleep while simultaneously tracking how the brain responds.

REM sleep, short for rapid eye movement sleep, is the stage when most vivid dreaming occurs. It also plays an important role in processing emotions, consolidating memories, and adapting to stress. Disturbances in this stage of sleep have been associated with several mental health conditions, making it an important target for latest treatments.

Sources indicate that "This is the first time we've been able to noninvasively target deep brain regions involved in REM sleep, while simultaneously monitoring brain activity," said Kai Wing "Kevin" Tang, a recent UT biomedical engineering Ph.D. graduate who led the research effort.

"Our skin-attached NEUSLeeP patch opens up newly introduced possibilities for understanding sleep and treating sleep disorders in home settings," added Huiliang "Evan" Wang, assistant professor in the Cockrell School of Engineering's Department of Biomedical Engineering. Wang supervised Tang's research and served as the principal investigator (PI) overseeing the project.

Sleep Patch Helps People Reach REM Sleep 43 Minutes Faster.

The early results suggest that the technology can make a measurable difference in how people experience REM sleep.

In a study involving 28 participants, published in Nature Communications, people using the patch entered REM sleep an average of 43 minutes sooner and spent approximately 16 additional minutes in that stage.

It has been revealed that these improvements were observed in both healthy sleepers and participants experiencing certain sleep difficulties. The volunteers also reported that the patch was comfortable to wear, with minimal adverse effects.

Unlike medications that affect the body more broadly, NEUSLeeP is designed to deliver stimulation to specific brain regions involved in sleep regulation. It uses ultrasound, a form of sound energy with frequencies beyond human hearing, to reach areas beneath the surface of the brain without requiring an invasive procedure.

The findings are encouraging, although the relatively small study means that larger trials will be needed to determine how consistently the technology works and whether its benefits persist over time.

Potential Benefits for Stress and Emotional Health.

The researchers also found evidence that the patch's effects may extend beyond increasing REM sleep.

It has been revealed that among healthy participants, ultrasound stimulation improved heart rate variability, a measure of the natural differences in time between consecutive heartbeats. This measurement provides insight into how the body's nervous system responds to stress and adjusts to changing conditions.

Industry observers note that brain imaging revealed changes in neural circuits involved in emotional processing. Together, these findings suggest that improving REM sleep through targeted stimulation could potentially support emotional regulation and the ability to cope with stress.

"REM sleep is not just about dreaming -- it's about emotional reset and stress adaptation," explained Gregory Fonzo, assistant professor in the Dell Medical School's Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and one of the project's co-PIs. "By enhancing REM, we may help people better cope with stress and improve their overall well-being.".

These possibilities are especially interesting because REM sleep disturbances have been linked to depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

Current approaches to sleep problems often involve medication or behavioral therapy. Although these treatments can be effective, medications may produce unwanted side effects, and existing approaches do not always directly address the biological processes responsible for disrupted REM sleep.

A device capable of influencing those processes without drugs or surgery could therefore offer an additional treatment option. However, the researchers have not yet established whether NEUSLeeP can improve symptoms of mental health disorders.

A Newly introduced Direction for Treating Insomnia and PTSD.

Building on the initial findings, the research team aims to conduct larger clinical trials to confirm the patch's effects and investigate its potential use in people with PTSD, depression, and chronic insomnia.

Beyond treating sleep disorders, the technology could eventually support sleep monitoring at home and provide scientists with a newly introduced way to study how deep brain regions influence sleep. Researchers also envision personalized therapies that could be adjusted to individual sleep patterns and needs.

"Our vision is a future where patients with mental health disorders can optimize their sleep with a noninvasive and safe treatment," remarked Vincent Mysliwiec, M.D., a professor at UT Health San Antonio, a leading expert in sleep disorders, and another co-PI on the project. "This technology could help millions of people get the restorative sleep they need.".

The team is already taking steps toward making NEUSLeeP available beyond the research setting. Working with the university's commercialization unit, Discovery to Impact, the researchers are exploring how to bring the device to market and have filed a patent application covering the technology.

If future studies confirm the early results, this wearable ultrasound patch could become a valuable fresh tool for improving REM sleep and potentially addressing conditions associated with poor sleep.

It has been revealed that other members of the research team include William D. Moscoso-Barrera, Mengxia Yu, Mengmeng Yao, Jinmo Jeong, Ilya Pyatnitskiy, Anakaren Romero Lozano, Jiachen Wang, Ju-Chun Hsieh, Tony Sungjin Chae, Daniel Song, Julieta Garcia, Rithvik Mittapalli, and Adam Bush of the Department of Biomedical Engineering; Benjamin Baird of the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Psychology; and Wynn Legon of Virginia Tech's Fralin Biomedical Research Institute.

Materials provided by University of Texas at Austin. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you’re in downtown Los Angeles now through November 29 and want to get an up-close-and-personal look at some cool cars, head over to the convention center to see what’s poppin’ at the annual auto show. However, if you don’t have time to make the trip—or you’re nowhere near L.A.—and want to see the best cars that this year’s event had to offer, we've got you covered. While the 2026 L.A. auto show was short on major debuts or futuristic concepts, it hosted several headline-catching cars as well as multiple highly anticipated new models.

It’s one thing to see the Tesla Roadster through your smartphone screen; it’s another thing to see it about six feet away. While we’re highly skeptical that Tesla will ever publicly sell the thruster-equipped version that flew through the air and did a barrel roll, it’s more likely that a similar-looking, street-legal version will eventually reach production. Haters gonna hate, but the Roadster looks pretty damn cool, like Lamborghini designer Fabrizio Giugiaro was hired to style his version of the Lotus Esprit S1 that James Bond drove in The Spy Who Loved Me. Consider us shaken, not stirred.

Being in the same room as a Bugatti EB110 is about as common as being in the same room as Sir Anthony Hopkins. Like meeting the actor who famously played Hannibal Lecter, meeting one of the most iconic supercars ever made is unnerving. Now, you may have noticed that this example isn’t exactly all original; instead, it has been modified by Phiaro Inc., and it features a custom widebody kit as well as a chameleon-like paint job. The best part? Its modifications are completely reversible. Let’s just say it drew a crowd.

Recent findings suggest that genesis is going after the throats of luxury stalwarts like BMW, Mercedes-Benz and—dare we say—Bentley with the latest GV90. The one you see here is the top-of-the-line Neolun model, and its most distinctive feature is these gigantic coach doors. Inside are four VIP-grade seats that treat passengers to an opulent cabin awash in rich materials and front seats that swivel 180 degrees to create a mobile lounge (this configuration is only accessible when the 657-hp EV is parked). The GV90 Neolun also has a veneer wood floor and 24-inch wheels that remind us of the iconic monoblock wheels made famous by Mercedes-AMG and Brabus. Few SUVs turn our heads, but Genesis appears to have another game-changer on its metaphorical hands.

Toyota Crown Signia GT-S Concept.

We spotted this beautiful wagon-like Toyota Crown Signia from across the convention center’s south hall. Among a sea of generic crossovers, this low-slung longroof is an ode to an age when most Americans didn’t lust after the elevated seating position of a semi-truck. Of course, if you haven’t noticed, this isn’t exactly a production-spec Crown Signia. If you read our recent SEMA coverage, you may recognize it as the GT-S concept. Along with being lowered by five inches and wearing flared fenders that resemble the Mustang GTD, it has custom one-off coil-over dampers, 21-inch HRE wheels, and brakes from a Lexus RX500h F Sport. To all that, we say, “Hell yeah, brother!”.

Sources indicate that let’s take a break from the world of flying cars, Bugattis, and fanciful electric SUVs to enjoy something that most people can afford: the new eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra. If its disorienting front lighting, heavily creased bodywork, and broad haunches intimidate you, we’re sure there’s a safer-looking alternative in Toyota’s showroom. But whatever you may think about the new Elantra’s styling, it definitely attracts attention. And Hyundai is hoping it’ll do just that to new customers who are looking to join the brand’s family tree. The nonhybrid version seen here draws power from a humble 147-hp four-cylinder engine, but the lineup will add a more powerful hybrid model sometime next year. While pricing is still TBD, we expect that it’ll cost around $25,000 to own the most interesting car in your cul-de-sac.

Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition.

If you’ve ever watched an episode of Overhaulin’, a TV show that lasted for 10 seasons on TLC, then you’ve heard of custom car designer Chip Foose. Now, he has teamed up with Fox Factory Vehicles to create this even more muscular version of the newly introduced Ram 1500 Rumble Bee street truck. Along with unique wheels and body graphics, the interior has been restyled with diamond-stitched seats and Foose branding. The truck itself has a lowered ride height with an aftermarket coil-over suspension, and its supercharged V-8 is available with either 705 or 1000 horsepower. That’s a lot of horsies, and they’ll cost customers a lot of cash, with the Rumble Bee Foose Edition starting at $154,990.

It has been revealed that this was one of the few concept cars at the show, but the Acura Nexera was first revealed back in August during Monterey Car Week. Still, the futuristic concept is really cool to see in person, especially with its dramatic glass canopy. Plus, how many times have you seen an Acura with butterfly doors? While the Nexera doesn’t preview an upcoming production model, it does provide a glimpse of Acura’s next-generation design language. Will the new 2028 RDX feature an active rear spoiler, carbon-fiber accents, and lighting that glows through the bodywork? Probably not. However, we can expect to see some of the Nexera concept’s interesting styling influence the brand’s next-gen compact SUV.

Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition.

In a recent development, if you’re old enough to remember Acura’s legendary DC2 Integra Type R, you’ll definitely appreciate this new Integra Type S Heritage Edition. Not only does its Blazing Phoenix Yellow call more attention to itself than Big Bird starring in an old-timey picture show, but it also honors the OG Type R, which also wore a shade of Phoenix Yellow. The modern-day throwback sport compact packs the same 320-hp turbo four and six-speed manual as other models, but this one alone has copper-colored wheels and a titanium shift knob from the Honda Civic Type R. To get one in your driveway, you’ll need to be lucky enough to score one of the 700 limited copies for the U.S. market, but the asking price is a reasonable $58,995.

Have you been waiting for Dodge to stuff a Hemi V-8 in the latest Charger? Well, you’re going to have to keep waiting for a while. However, if you’ve been hoping that the Brotherhood of Muscle will make a gas-powered Charger that’s set up for quick lap times, the new Super Bee variant should help you scratch that itch. Along with exclusive aero bits, stronger brakes, and wider summer tires, this track-focused Charger features an enhanced high-output Hurricane twin-turbo 3.0-liter straight-six, which is good for 600 horsepower (50 more than normal). The reimagined “Super Bee” logo on the rear quarter panel is one way to separate it from its siblings, but it also has an entirely different front clip that features new headlights and more open space to inhale engine-cooling air. If you’re wondering how much it costs, so are we, so stay tuned.

It has been revealed that like many of you, this was our first time seeing the fresh Chevy Silverado 1500’s new off-road-focused ZR2 variant. It’s a massive truck, so big that we initially thought it was the HD version. Among the many changes to the newest generation of Chevy’s bestselling full-size pickup truck are all-new small-block V-8s. The ZR2 seen here is powered by a 481-hp 6.6-liter that helps churn massive all-terrain tires, which now stand 35 inches tall for the first time on a half-ton Silverado. The Ford F-150 Raptor-rivaling ZR2’s other party tricks include trick Multimatic DSSV spool-valve dampers. Inside, it includes GM’s first use of forged carbon fiber (neat!). If you want the most badass version, you’ll want to opt for the Bison Edition that adds beadlock-capable wheels, unique bumpers, and even more underbody armor. The cost of admission for the regular ZR2 is just under $80K, while the Bison starts even higher.

Recent findings suggest that eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive fresh cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage presently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find newly introduced jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

According to recent reports, despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, losing progress in a game is never fun, but imagine spending 11 hours exploring Grand Theft Auto 6 only to discover that none of it was saved. That's exactly what happened to content creator JasonTheWeen, who had a particularly rough launch day after making one unfortunate mistake with his PlayStation 5.

With around 1.3 million followers on YouTube, the content creator had been streaming an extended session of Rockstar's latest adventure. However, after accidentally turning off his console, he returned to the game only to find that his entire 11-hour save was missing!

According to recent reports, according to The Economic Times, he later explained that his foot had accidentally hit the switch on an extension cord, cutting power to his PS5. The moment he realized what had happened was captured live, and his reaction was understandably heartbreaking. Here, take a look:.

Visibly devastated, the streamer struggled to hold back tears and repeatedly shouted about the 11 hours he had just lost. He then contacted someone from his team to ask whether there was any way to recover his progress, even if that meant getting back to the beginning of the second chapter rather than having to start the entire adventure again.

Unfortunately, it seems that it wasn’t possible, and he eventually brought a friend to help him rush through the sections he had already completed, hoping to get his marathon back on track.

Sources indicate that the exact reason behind the incident remains unclear, but there's a possible explanation involving the game's save system. GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain important events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

In a recent development, one possibility is that JasonTheWeen accidentally turned off his PS5 while the game was writing save data. If that happened, interrupting the process could have corrupted the save file, potentially explaining why so much progress disappeared when he launched the game again.

GTA 6 does feature autosaving, which records progress after completing missions and certain important events. But that doesn't necessarily mean every action is immediately stored.

Industry observers note that it's notable to stress that this is only a theory, and neither Rockstar nor the streamer has confirmed what actually caused the loss. We also don't know whether the save can be recovered, so it would be unfair to draw conclusions about the game's autosave system based on this single incident.

Still, the situation is a good reminder that manually saving your progress is worth the extra few seconds. GTA 6 offers multiple manual save slots, allowing players to keep separate backups instead of relying exclusively on autosaving. This can be particularly useful after completing a long mission or spending hours exploring Leonida.

For anyone planning to sink an entire afternoon into the game, taking a moment to create a manual save might save you from a very unpleasant surprise later!

Sources indicate that unfortunately, losing his progress wasn't the only upsetting moment JasonTheWeen experienced during the stream. Shortly afterward, he heard shouting outside his home and informed viewers that police officers had arrived at his property.

Sources indicate that the incident appears to have been a case of swatting, a dangerous prank involving false emergency reports intended to send police officers to someone's home. It's an especially unpleasant situation for any streamer, and it made an already frustrating day considerably worse.

In a recent development, following the incident, JasonTheWeen also reached out to Rockstar and Sony on social media, asking whether his lost progress could be recovered. For now, there's no confirmed response from either company about his request or why all the progress was lost.
