📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is finally time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5 as we open the doors for Grand Theft Auto 6. This doesn’t mean that we didn’t have some good times with GTA 5, but all good things must eventually come to an end.

Sources indicate that now that we are turning to the next chapter, we have to look back on GTA 5 with a fond smile and tearful eyes. Some of the best memories for people were made with that game. Communities came together, lawsuits were filed, and more.

GTA 5 had a massive impact on the world, and it is now time to reflect on the game before booting up GTA 6 and moving on.

Recent findings suggest that there are multiple memes that were spawned thanks to GTA 5. For instance, Trevor kidnapping a guy’s wife will always live rent free in my head, but one of the biggest was the “Davey, how you doing,” meme.

According to recent reports, the scene is simple; Michael just meets up with Davey at the observatory. Well, this sparked a massive collection of memes, and it was mostly thanks to the ability to initiate the cutscene in different ways.

Sources indicate that people started reenacting the cutscene in real life, and doing absurd things in game like crashing a blimp into the observatory to initiate the cutscene. It will forever remain in people’s minds.

It has been revealed that while yes, GTA 6 is now here, that doesn’t mean that GTA 5 is gone. While people may be leaving the story behind, the online mode still exists, and it is still one of the most popular online games that exist.

It is estimated that there are around 8.5 to 10 million active users in GTA Online each week, and they aren’t going to just abandon the online because of GTA 6, at least not while there isn’t a new GTA Online to flock to.

According to recent reports, GTA 5 will continue to live on through the online mode for the next year until the next iteration of GTA Online is released. At that point, I may have to write another article.

Grand Theft Auto 5 is the first and only game in the GTA series to have three protagonists: Michael, Trevor, and Franklin. Many people were concerned about there being three protagonists because it might dilute each character.

Sources indicate that to everyone’s surprise, it didn’t dilute any of the characters, and it instead enhanced them. The characters work off each other, and it helped build the narrative.

Industry observers note that despite it being 13 years, there are people who still remember quotes from the game. People can describe full scenes and story beats. It is pretty amazing. That type of dedication never goes away. It’s similar to the adults who can still quote early episodes of SpongeBob.

Sources indicate that can we take a moment to reflect on how many copies of GTA 5 were sold worldwide? The game sold approximately 235 million copies within the last 13 years. This is one of the most sold games in the history of gaming.

That type of legacy doesn’t just go away. Only a few games have sold more copies than GTA 5, and they include Minecraft and Tetris. That is a very impressive feat.

Recent findings suggest that up until this year, kids have begged their parents to purchase them GTA 5, and adults have caved in to see what the hype was all about. With it being as significant as it was, GTA 5 will never be forgotten. It will go down in gaming history and that is a fact.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 5 isn’t going to be forgotten anytime soon, and if you want proof, look at the current sales. I don’t mean the sales numbers over the last 13 years, I mean the sales numbers from the last week or so.

It has been revealed that within the last quarter, it is estimated that Rockstar sold another 5 million copies of GTA 5. That is ridiculous when you consider that the game is 13 years old.

The hype around GTA 6 has been increasing sales for past GTA titles, but it has mostly had the effect of increasing the sales number of GTA 5, which means that people will still be playing the story for the next year while they wait for GTA Online 2.0 to be released.

Grand Theft Auto 5 was released during a time when people still got together to play games. While the main focus is connecting with people online, there are many who got together during the time of GTA 5 and played the game together in the same room.

Sources indicate that parties were formed, and people played the game together. They formed a bond, and that bond carried over into GTA Online, where people continued to play together and make memories.

These memories are still with those who played the game together and continue to enjoy the online. I played online with multiple friends and I will forever remember those times we shared before the next evolution of the online is released.

Recent findings suggest that the Grand Theft Auto series is record-breaking, and there is no doubt about that. GTA 5 alone broke multiple records, and that is something that people won’t forget.

As far as records go, GTA 5 broke the record for highest-24 hour entertainment revenue, best-selling video game in 24 hours, best-selling action-adventure game in 24 hours, highest grossing video game in 24 hours, fastest game to reach $1billion in revenue, and more.

According to recent reports, when the game rolled out, it was a huge deal, and it demonstrates through the number of copies that were sold, and it shows even more through the number of records that were broken by it. In total, it broke at least eight records. I can’t think of another game that has done that, and now it is GTA 6’s turn.

Recent findings suggest that whenever a massive game comes out that parodies stuff in real life, it is bound to attract a few lawsuits, and boy was GTA 5 the center of quite a few lawsuits over the years. One of the earlier ones was from Daz Dillinger who issued a cease and desist letter.

After that, other celebrities like Lindsay Lohan and Karen Gravano filed lawsuits against Rockstar over GTA 5, with one being over an alleged likeness and the other being about a character who mirrored their life.

Recent findings suggest that there was even once a lawsuit over GTA Online because it didn’t launch with the release of the game and was instead released some time later. While it isn’t the best look, this attention still attracts people to the game and it makes people remember the name.

Industry observers note that do you believe that violent video games make people more violent in real life? Many don’t believe so, but there is a sect of those who think there is a link between violent behavior and video games, especially when the game has carjackings, murder, and other criminal activities.

In 2021, GTA V was mentioned in law HB3531 filed in Illinois. The goal of this law was to prohibit the sale of games featuring “psychological harm.” Ultimately, it wanted to restrict the sale of games like GTA 5 that featured criminal activity, meaning GTA 5 would get banned.

This wasn’t the first time the series came under fire from lawmakers, and it probably won’t be the last, but it leaves a lasting impression that people still remember and will help GTA 5 live on.

Breaking: Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1372 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.
  • Recent findings suggest that you haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics.
  • According to recent reports, I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

Recent findings suggest that you haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

According to recent reports, I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

It has been revealed that presently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

Recent findings suggest that my computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw promptly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

It has been revealed that I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is introduced over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

Sources indicate that I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

Sources indicate that the screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

According to recent reports, the worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Sources indicate that casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

According to recent reports, europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

Industry observers note that china will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

Sources indicate that first Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

Industry observers note that the change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet stated how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

In a recent development, worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

For LEC teams, clarity on the season opener in China is due in January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's all or nothing in Outfit7's latest update for Talking Tom Gold Run, where the concept of "high risk, high return" has never been truer! In particular, a new Extraction Mode within the endless runner tasks you with running faster and faster for better and better rewards - the catch is that when you crash and burn, so does your hard-earned haul.

The limited-time event not only challenges your quick reflexes but also your prudence - do you go for the bigger pay-off or leave while you can with what you already have? There are three chances for you to tap out, and once you reach each extraction point, you get to choose whether or not you want to stick around.

The thing is, if you choose to keep going, the faster the run gets, making obstacles trickier to dodge. Wacky Planet's fast-paced side world offers a little bit of mercy as an indicator tells you how far the next extraction point is - but even so, the gold bars, character cards, and diamonds (which appear later in the run) might just get farther out of reach too.

There's a handy Save Me option you can opt for when you fail, giving you a chance to revive and continue your run. It's a true test of tapping talent, so it's only fitting you get four new outfits to go along with it!

Tang Suit Ginger, Mooncake Ginger, Moonlight Angela and Hanfu Angela join in to spice up the theming, so if you'd like to look the part while dashing through the newly introduced mode, now's your chance.

If you're all set to win big or lose it all, Talking Tom Gold Run's latest event is now live on iOS and Android, and you can download the endless runner for free to get started!

Sources indicate that download now! Talking Tom Gold Run.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending revision has been officially detailed.
  • Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.
  • Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller upgrade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending revision has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller upgrade. When Battlefield Studios revealed it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

In a recent development, the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a massive focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

According to recent reports, interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

It has been revealed that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

It has been revealed that finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

#29252. Tech Report: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?

Tech Report: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and important pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.
  • Industry observers note that research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions.
  • According to recent reports, these medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Medications like Ozempic and Wegovy, which contain semaglutide — a GLP‑1 receptor agonist that helps regulate blood sugar, appetite and body weight — have become household names and important pillars in obesity management for the medical profession.

Industry observers note that research has shown GLP-1 medications reduce body weight by an average of 15 percent when used weekly for 68 weeks and combined with lifestyle interventions. This is because semaglutide acts on the brain to increase the feeling of fullness and to decrease appetite.

According to recent reports, these medications don’t work the same way for everyone, however. Our multidisciplinary research team at the University of Alberta is working to improve obesity care for people of all ages and to understand why some people respond better to semaglutide than others, and how their weight loss can be maintained over time.

We are investigating the role of energy metabolism as a potentially important piece in a complex puzzle.

It has been revealed that research has shown semaglutide medications to improve quality of life, blood markers such as sugar or cholesterol, strength and overall health. Weight loss is only one measure of how well they work.

We are exploring whether people’s responses to these medications could lie in individual factors such as genetics, metabolism, body composition, lifestyle, microbiota, associated diseases, age and sex.

Recent findings suggest that energy metabolism may also be an key piece of this puzzle. This is a measure of the total calories consumed (in) and the total calories burned (out). We burn calories all the time: for vital processes like breathing and thinking, physical activities like going to the gym and the everyday act of digesting food.

It has been revealed that when we lose weight, our bodies naturally need less energy. But sometimes, the body goes into an extra “energy-saving mode,” burning even fewer calories than we would expect. This is called metabolic adaptation, or adaptive thermogenesis.

Sources indicate that think of it like a light bulb that automatically dims to save electricity. This is one reason why losing weight can become more difficult over time, sometimes leading to a weight-loss plateau.

Recent findings suggest that changes in body weight and composition (the amount of fat and fat-free mass in our bodies) play an notable role in energy metabolism. Both fat and fat-free mass use energy, even when we are resting. As we lose these tissues, our bodies naturally burn fewer calories.

Recent findings suggest that researchers are still trying to understand whether weight-loss medications influence these processes differently. If we can understand how our bodies use energy during and after weight loss, this could help us develop better strategies for maintaining weight loss over the long term.

Sources indicate that we published a recent review of studies investigating the effects of GLP-1 therapies on energy utilization. We found a few studies exploring how semaglutide affects resting energy use, with findings that were neutral or inconclusive.

The question of how semaglutide impacts energy use is an emerging area of study, and remains an open question for exploration.

At the University of Alberta, we have a gold-standard method to measure energy utilization called a whole-room indirect calorimeter. This is a rare research facility and is similar to a hotel suite that can precisely measure each component of energy use. This room can isolate the effects of changes in someone’s calorie burning at rest, after eating and during exercise.

It has been revealed that we are presently recruiting research participants with blood sugar regulation problems, such as insulin resistance or diabetes, who are about to start semaglutide treatment. We will follow their weight loss journey over six months to investigate changes in body weight and composition, and energy utilization using sophisticated approaches.

Understanding how semaglutide influences energy use and body composition, and how these changes interact, could be an important step toward explaining why individuals respond differently to weight-loss treatment.

Sources indicate that this will allow us to contribute to more personalized approaches to obesity and Type 2 diabetes management in the future. Having a better understanding of how energy use changes with semaglutide-induced weight loss will also help us to better anticipate potential non-responders (people who do not lose weight) and offer alternative treatments sooner in their health journey.

Importantly, current evidence suggests that if you are taking semaglutide or considering starting treatment, you should make a few lifestyle changes.

According to recent reports, materials provided by The Conversation. Original written by Giovanna Guimaraes Lopes Bergamasco, Andrea M. Haqq, Carla Prado, and Rachel J. Skow. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Latest Update: Powerful upcoming weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1166 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle.
  • The two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total.
  • The benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For people living with painful knee osteoarthritis (OA), even simple activities like walking, climbing stairs, or getting out of a chair can become a struggle. Excess body weight can make these challenges even worse. Now, two major clinical trials suggest that a powerful experimental weight-loss drug could provide substantial relief.

The two phase 3 trials, led by Northwestern University, included more than 1,000 participants in total. People receiving the highest dose of retatrutide, an experimental injectable weight-loss medication, lost an average of about 25% of their body weight. When researchers combined the findings from both trials, they found that approximately two-thirds of participants treated with retatrutide reported a reduction in knee pain of at least 50%. By comparison, only 38% of those given a placebo experienced that level of relief.

The benefits extended beyond weight loss and improved knee pain. Participants also revealed reductions in blood pressure, blood lipid levels, and inflammation throughout the body.

Recent findings suggest that findings from both studies were published on Nov. 8 in the New England Journal of Medicine.

Sources indicate that "The findings are really saying for people who are overweight and have OA, if you lose a significant amount of weight with this treatment, there is a good chance that you're going to get a meaningful reduction in your knee pain," remarked corresponding author Dr. Thomas Schnitzer, professor of physical medicine and rehabilitation, anesthesiology and medicine (rheumatology) at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.

"A major factor is that you're loading your knees less and therefore, there's less pain and it allows you to increase your function.".

Philip Conaghan, a study co-author and professor of musculoskeletal medicine at the University of Leeds in the United Kingdom, presented results from one of the trials, TRIUMPH-4, on Nov. 8 at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in Orlando, Florida. Findings from the second trial, TRIUMPH-1-OA, were scheduled for presentation during a separate poster session that same day.

A Potential New Treatment for Millions With Knee Osteoarthritis.

Sources indicate that painful knee osteoarthritis affects approximately 5% of Americans (15 million people). Available treatments range from physical therapy and medications applied to the skin to oral anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen and Voltaren. Other options include opioids and corticosteroid injections, although the relief provided by steroid injections generally lasts only a short time.

In a recent development, weight loss is another established way to ease symptoms. Previous studies have shown that losing 5% to 10% of body weight through changes in diet and exercise can improve knee osteoarthritis pain. However, Schnitzer explained that losing more than 10% through these approaches alone is often challenging. For people already struggling with painful knees, exercising enough to achieve substantial weight loss can be especially difficult.

According to recent reports, retatrutide could offer another approach. Developed by Eli Lilly, the experimental medication is administered as a once-weekly injection and works differently from existing GLP-1 medications such as semaglutide and tirzepatide.

Industry observers note that while those drugs act on one or two hormone receptors and typically produce weight reductions of 10% to 20%, retatrutide activates receptors associated with three different naturally occurring hormones. In the clinical trials, participants lost approximately 20% to 25% of their body weight, depending on the dose. Eli Lilly scientists also contributed to the research as study co-authors.

Industry observers note that "Participants had remarkable responses," Schnitzer stated. "Many of the people in this study lost considerable amounts of weight, with a few losing up to a hundred pounds or more.".

Why Diet and Exercise Still Matter.

Despite the encouraging findings, Schnitzer emphasized that lifestyle changes should remain the starting point for people who are overweight and have painful knee osteoarthritis.

It has been revealed that improving eating habits, increasing physical activity, and making other sustainable lifestyle adjustments can help reduce symptoms without the expense of newer weight-loss medications. These strategies also avoid side effects associated with GLP-1 drugs, including gastrointestinal problems and muscle loss.

Sources indicate that maintaining muscle strength is particularly important for people with knee osteoarthritis because the muscles surrounding the joint help support and stabilize it. Losing too much muscle could therefore create additional challenges for patients who already have difficulty moving comfortably.

Industry observers note that for individuals who cannot achieve sufficient weight loss through lifestyle changes and continue to experience significant knee pain, Schnitzer believes retatrutide could become a valuable option if it receives approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Could the Drug Also Slow Knee Arthritis Progression?

Although the trials demonstrated substantial improvements in weight and pain, several vital questions remain unanswered.

According to recent reports, one of the biggest is whether retatrutide does more than relieve symptoms. Researchers still do not know if the drug can slow the underlying progression of knee osteoarthritis enough to reduce the likelihood that patients will eventually need knee replacement surgery. People who already required a knee replacement were excluded from the trials.

"That would be the goal here to say you can reduce people's pain, and you can stop the progression of their osteoarthritis," Schnitzer remarked.

Industry observers note that another unanswered question is whether retatrutide might benefit people with painful knee osteoarthritis who are not overweight. Because the trials did not include these patients, further studies will be needed to determine whether they could experience similar improvements.

Researchers are also interested in understanding how much of the pain relief comes directly from weight loss and how much might be related to the drug's effects on inflammation.

Industry observers note that "These drugs are believed to have significant anti-inflammatory activity, but the mechanism is not entirely known," Schnitzer remarked. "Whether cutting down inflammation in the joint is also important in addition to reducing load needs more research, so this is still a first step, in my view. I've been working in the OA field for a long time, and I think this opens up opportunities to do a lot more studies to understand the condition better.".

How Researchers Measured Knee Pain Relief.

To evaluate changes in symptoms, the research teams used the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC) Pain index, a standardized tool for assessing osteoarthritis pain.

It has been revealed that during study visits, participants rated their pain on a scale from 0 to 10. They also used a mobile app to record their pain levels each day, allowing researchers to track how symptoms changed throughout treatment.

The study is titled, "Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity.".

Materials provided by Northwestern University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Latest Update: GTA 6 Made 2 Million XBOX Players Lie About Their Nationality

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.
  • Recent findings suggest that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and promptly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64.
  • According to recent reports, or not.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game about criminals, which might explain why millions of XBOX players technically broke their terms of service and lied about their nationality, all just to play the game a little earlier.

Recent findings suggest that there’s no denying that Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of 2026, selling millions of copies ahead of launch, and promptly becoming tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, matched only by the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64. As such, millions of people were waiting at midnight on November 19, when the game became available in their region.

According to recent reports, or not. It turns out that millions of XBOX players jumped the queue and decided to lie to boot up Grand Theft Auto 6 early. This is thanks to a trick that’s much easier to pull off on XBOX than PlayStation 5, prompting lots of people to change their nationality.

According to recent reports, A report by Ampere Analysis (with thanks to Eurogamer) has revealed that over two million XBOX players used the “Latest Zealand trick” to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early. 100,000 PlayStation 5 consumers did something similar, but that method was more difficult, which is why the number is much smaller.

Sources indicate that the New Zealand trick has been used for many significant releases on XBOX systems in the past. Because of time zone differences, most video games launch in New Zealand first. If a player changes their XBOX system settings to New Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

Sources indicate that the PlayStation 5 version of the trick involves creating a separate account with billing information, which is a massive pain in the neck, which explains why only 100,000 people bothered. The Fresh Zealand XBOX trick literally takes a minute to pull off and is easy to revert afterward.

If a player changes their XBOX system settings to Upcoming Zealand, then they can access the country’s version of the Microsoft Store, and in the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, they were able to play it over twelve hours earlier.

Some fans were concerned that Microsoft would ban accounts that did the Upcoming Zealand trick. After all, it breaks the Microsoft Store's terms of service. However, many official XBOX social media accounts playfully encouraged people to do it, as it was essentially a free win for the brand, at a time when it badly needed one. As it stands, there are reports of bans, even now that the trick isn’t necessary, so there's no need for anyone to worry about switching flags.

Sources indicate that while the New Zealand trick is well-known among fans, and is something many gaming outlets will gleefully inform the public about ahead of a big release, it’s usually only done by a small audience. Grand Theft Auto 6 is such a massive game that more people than usual temporarily became Kiwis, giving them an early chance to play.

Now that Grand Theft Auto 6 is out, it’s unclear what the next major game will have a similar effect. 2027 has some massive hits, but it would be hard to claim any will be as important as Grand Theft Auto VI. If Persona 6 manages to launch in 2027, then the JRPG audience on XBOX might all take a journey to Mordor, but it’ll be unlikely that millions will do so.

Updated on November 19th, 2026 - reformatted and rechecked the list With GTA VI now finally in the hands of players, a decade-plus wait is finally over. But what if you're going to be without your console or PC for a while? How exactly do you get that hit of open-world action when you can't find GTA VI on mobile (yet)?

Industry observers note that well, that's where we come in, with our list of the best mobile games like Grand Theft Auto; covering a huge variety of open-world, crime-focused action games. And, luckily enough, plenty of the classic GTAs are also already on mobile!

Yes, while Grove Street Games' mobile ports may be considered a bit lacklustre by some, they're still well-loved for bringing some of the greatest console classics to mobile. And we'll get to them in due course!

Arguably the only 'true' competitor to Grand Theft Auto that saw any measure of success near their level, Saints Row always dove into the wackier, stranger and more glitzy sides of street culture. And with the Third Street Saints ditching their humble origins, when they're brought back to earth, it's up to you to once more become kings of crime in the brand-fresh city of Steelport.

Whether it's flopping off of car hoods to defraud insurance, battling zombies with an oversized marital aid or simply speeding through the air on your jet-bike (Volition did it first), Saints Row: The Third offers exciting open-world crime action on mobile that's almost on par with the best GTA has to offer.

It has been revealed that A real gem of Rockstar's back catalogue, when it seemed as if they always had something experimental up their sleeve before their attention turned solely to Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption. Bully: Anniversary Edition is a game that was massively controversial as well as beloved by fans.

Set in Bullworth Academy, you play reckless delinquent Jimmy as you navigate the various social cliques, overbearing administration and tedious lessons inflicted on you. And along the way, maybe, just maybe, you'll turn the world of Bullworth upside down in a way no one will forget.

When Rockstar decided they wanted to dust off their quirky, spaghetti-western shooter Red Dead Revolver and give it a brand-newly introduced GTA-style makeover, I think few expected it to be as popular as it became.

Recent findings suggest that playing as John Marston, you'll ride the range of the American West in pursuit of your former comrades-in-crime, with the intent of saving your family and maybe your own soul along the way. Expect shootouts, bank robberies, cattle rustling and maybe a few zombies along the way.

One of many GTA Online-likes to try and recreate the open-world crime experience on mobile, just with fewer Shark Cards, Grand Outlaws is another recent release well worth looking into. While its more colourful setting may clash with what you expect from a gritty crime thriller, and it looks more Fortnite than Sleeping Dogs, it's still got plenty of appeal for those wanting something GTA-style in their lives.

Probably one of the largest-scale competitors in the GTA Online-likes scene, OneState is one to go for if you prefer a more realistic interpretation of open-world crime and action than Grand Outlaws. Its realistic recreation of Los Angeles even boasts a near-future, plausible version of real-life developments.

About the only thing to be aware of when it comes to OneState is that this is an RP game first and foremost, and you'll be just as likely to fall into the role of firefighter or EMT as a crime kingpin. But if that depth of realism is what you're hunting for, OneState is sure to satisfy.

Recent findings suggest that A really unique (as much as my editors hate using that word) entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, Chinatown Wars takes you back to Liberty City. But rather than exploring the mafia connections, you'll be joining the deadly world of the triads.

Set from a top-down perspective like the classic entries in the series, Chinatown Wars boasts interesting minigames, the same level of violence and chaos as you'd expect, as well as a sprawling narrative of revenge and ambition.

Download now! Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars Max Payne.

Recent findings suggest that are we breaking from the trend of 'open world' here? Sure, absolutely. But Max Payne, first released by Remedy and later acquired by Rockstar, is undoubtedly full of the same gunplay and thrilling crime storylines as any GTA entry. And, I'd argue, that its actual gunplay is leagues ahead of what Grand Theft Auto has ever offered.

Sources indicate that set in Fresh York during the middle of a snowstorm, you play as the gritty police detective Max Payne as you shoot your way through hordes of mafia goons. The bullet-time mechanic still holds up years later, and if you need a short, sharp hit of shootout action, then Max Payne is one to grab.

Download now! Max Payne Mobile Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories.

Sources indicate that another one-off entry in the brief portable series that Rockstar had, which includes Vice City Stories (sadly not available on mobile). In Liberty City Stories, you return once more to the 3D incarnation of their Fresh York analogue, before it got a major makeover for Grand Theft Auto IV.

Recent findings suggest that playing as Toni Cipriani, you'll be working closely with the mafia and experience Liberty City and what it was like before Grand Theft Auto III. Definitely one to play if you were a fan of watching The Sopranos, and if you're just a major fan of delving into the history of GTA as a universe!

Recent findings suggest that and now for something completely different... Okay, not that different. But Neverness to Everness is undoubtedly one to play only if you're willing to really stretch the definition of a GTA-like. Rather than a realistic city or characters, you'll be jumping into anime-inspired action with flashy combat and a sprawling metropolis.

Industry observers note that but even if you are fighting on the right side of the law, Neverness to Everness tries to lean into the mayhem of GTA just as much as any other. And while it's had some controversial complications with AI, at its core it's still got plenty of the same fun to be had on the go as Grand Theft Auto.

According to recent reports, A Gameloft production for mobile, Gangstar Vegas may be the lesser pick on this list. But, purely for curiosity's sake it's well worth looking at for its ambition alone. Released back in 2013, Gangstar Vegas was arguably the first mobile game to try and match what GTA had to offer, full 3D world included.

Boasting all the same glitz, glamour and grime as GTA, not to mention the always-fun Las Vegas setting, Gangstar Vegas: World of Crime is rightly regarded as a flawed, but lovable cult classic that really highlights how difficult it is to pin down the formula. Still, it gets more than a few points for trying.

Download now! Gangstar Vegas Honourable Mention: Other GTA Ports If what you want is just GTA, name included, then mobile is pretty chock-a-block with them. We've got Vice City, San Andreas, Chinatown Wars and Grand Theft Auto III all available to play on your choice of iOS or Android. Not to mention the er, Definitive Edition ports too.

But, as you may well know, these are ports where a lot of rough edges can be seen. While not quite as shoddy as the infamous Definitive Collection, Grove Street Games' ports of the original 3D trilogy are definitely not the best way to experience them, but on mobile they're all feature-complete and almost as good as you remember them; keyword being 'almost'. And with that in mind, those are some of the best, if not the best, ways to experience GTA-like action on mobile while you're away from your console or PC! And if you want to relive the classics, you've also got options with the available ports. So, when you need to take a break from GTA VI, you're still spoilt for choice on mobile.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding new content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 enhancement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 revision to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are upcoming quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

According to recent reports, "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding new content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 enhancement. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

"The reason for this patch is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

As laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several newly introduced dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

More clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A newly introduced opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

Industry observers note that "All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

It has been revealed that you can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's update.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a new playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment.
  • In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups.
  • Cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that reading for enjoyment may offer far more than entertainment. Whether someone prefers a classic Jane Austen novel or a Heartstopper graphic novel, research suggests that reading for pleasure is associated with better mental health, stronger empathy, and a lower risk of dementia.

In a recent development, researchers at the University of Cambridge are working with The Queen's Reading Room, a charity established by Her Majesty The Queen, to raise awareness of these benefits across all age groups. Their collaboration is part of the National Year of Reading, an initiative encouraging more people to make reading part of their lives.

Cambridge psychiatry researchers Professor Barbara Sahakian and Dr. Christelle Langley began exploring the subject while writing their 2025 book, Brain Boost: Healthy Habits for a Happier Life. They discovered that reading for enjoyment was connected to a remarkably wide range of positive outcomes, yet the amount of research specifically examining these benefits was surprisingly limited.

In a review published in Psychological Medicine, Sahakian and Langley joined Vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, to examine the available evidence. Their findings suggest that the format and type of reading matter less than the enjoyment people get from it. They also highlight how reading together, whether through book clubs or parents sharing stories with children, can provide additional benefits.

Industry observers note that professor Sahakian said: "Reading is a great way to support our brain health, develop important cognitive skills and boost our well-being. It's something we ought to be encouraging from an early age, given the increasing evidence of its benefits, particularly to children, but really, it's never too late to start, and it can bring benefits throughout our lives and into old age.".

Reading Early in Life Is Linked to Better Brain Development.

Despite the growing evidence of its advantages, reading for enjoyment has become less common among young people. Surveys indicate that reading rates among children and teenagers have fallen to their lowest recorded levels, with particularly steep challenges among teenage boys and children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

Even children who are least enthusiastic about reading recognize that it can help them academically. Nearly half acknowledge that books and other reading materials can introduce them to unfamiliar words or teach them something upcoming.

One of the most compelling studies examined more than 10,000 young people. Conducted by Sahakian, Langley, and their colleagues, the research found that children who started reading for pleasure at an early age tended to perform better in several important areas. These included attention, memory, and executive functioning, the mental abilities involved in planning, decision-making, and managing behavior.

Early readers also showed stronger academic performance, experienced fewer mental health problems, and were more likely to develop healthier daily routines. In particular, they tended to get more sleep and spend less time using screens.

Dr. Langley noted: "Given how beneficial reading for pleasure is at a young age, we should be doing everything we can to introduce children and young people to reading. The notable thing is to find something they'd really enjoy reading about - it might be a TV program or a game - and use this as a way in. Reading comics and graphic novels could also be a helpful introduction as they might be seen as less intimidating, maybe less boring, than novels.".

The academic advantages may extend beyond language and literacy. Studies have also connected reading with stronger mathematical performance. Researchers suggest this relationship may arise because both activities rely on some of the same mental abilities, including language processing, memory, and executive function.

Just Five Minutes of Reading May Reduce Stress.

The benefits of reading do not disappear after childhood. Among adults, surveys have associated reading for enjoyment with improved emotional well-being, greater relaxation, and reduced stress. Readers also tend to report more empathy, a deeper understanding of other people, and greater openness to viewpoints different from their own.

For many people, books are an especially appealing way to unwind. Reading ranks as the most popular approach to stress relief, with nearly two in five adults (38%) identifying it as their preferred way to relax.

It has been revealed that A neuroscience study commissioned by The Queen's Reading Room in 2024 found that spending just five minutes reading fiction could lower stress by as much as 20%. The study also reported improvements in concentration and problem-solving abilities, along with a reduced sense of loneliness.

Sources indicate that books may even provide more comfort than some traditional relaxation habits. In one survey, more respondents said they turned to reading (35%) for comfort than to drinking wine (31%) or taking a hot bath (10%).

Reading Linked to Lower Dementia and Alzheimer's Risk.

It has been revealed that as people get older, the potential advantages of reading may become especially meaningful. Research has associated mentally stimulating leisure activities, including reading, with slower cognitive decline and a reduced likelihood of developing dementia.

Sources indicate that one study followed nearly 5,500 adults aged 55 and older for five years. Participants who regularly took part in activities such as reading were significantly less likely to develop cognitive impairment during the study period.

Another investigation reported an even more striking association. People who read newspapers, magazines, and books had a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

According to recent reports, these findings suggest that keeping the mind engaged through reading may support cognitive health in later life. However, the researchers emphasize that most of the available studies identify associations rather than proving that reading itself prevents dementia.

How Reading May Change the Structure of the Brain.

According to recent reports, what could explain the many benefits associated with reading? Brain imaging research offers some intriguing clues.

Studies have identified differences in brain structure associated with reading, particularly in regions responsible for language, learning, emotional regulation, and executive control. These differences include greater brain volume and larger cortical areas in certain regions, as well as thicker cortex in areas important for language processing.

Researchers have also observed stronger connections within the brain's white matter, which helps different regions communicate and supports the processing of language.

Although much of this evidence is correlational, some research suggests that reading-related training can directly influence the brain's physical structure.

According to recent reports, in one small study involving 11 children with dyslexia between the ages of 7 and 11, researchers tested an eight-week training program designed to strengthen reading abilities. The exercises involved mental imagery, articulation, and tracing letters, combinations of letters, and words.

Following the program, the children demonstrated significant improvements in reading skills. Brain scans also revealed increases in gray matter volume in notable regions, providing evidence that reading interventions can be accompanied by measurable structural changes in the brain.

Why Reading Together May Offer Even Greater Benefits.

Recent findings suggest that reading does not have to be a solitary activity. Researchers suggest that sharing books with other people can add a valuable social dimension, creating opportunities for connection and potentially improving both mental and physical well-being.

Recent findings suggest that the Queen's Reading Room has made this idea a central part of its mission. Launched on social media in January 2021, the initiative originally provided a way for people to exchange book recommendations and stay connected during pandemic lockdowns.

It has since expanded into an international community reaching more than 12 million people across 184 countries. Through its flagship festival, neuroscience research, and other programs, the charity works to make reading a more prominent part of everyday life.

Its activities also extend to homeless shelters and domestic violence refuges, where shared reading is used as a therapeutic resource to help people during recovery.

The social connections created through reading groups may be particularly valuable for older adults, who can face increased isolation and reduced opportunities to participate in physically demanding activities.

Industry observers note that professor Sahakian said: "Shared reading groups and book clubs appear to provide additional benefits through social interaction. They can help people feel less isolated and more connected to others, which has been shown to reduce the risk of dementia.

"While these clubs can be fun and beneficial at any age, they're perfect for older people who may not be so mobile - they might not be able to go out as an exercise group or a cycling group, but a reading group is something most people can enjoy.".

According to recent reports, the researchers' overall message is that people can benefit from reading at any stage of life. Whether someone enjoys novels, newspapers, comics, or stories shared with friends, making time for reading may help support cognitive health, emotional well-being, and social connection.

Recent findings suggest that vicki Perrin, CEO of The Queen's Reading Room, added: "At The Queen's Reading Room, we have seen first-hand the transformative power of individual and shared reading to change lives. Books truly do make life better, and we're excited to do our bit to help everyone, everywhere, make more room for reading.".

Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whether you like it or loathe it, there's no doubting the popularity and staying power of Monopoly Go for Scopely. Now, the hit tabletop-to-mobile adaptation is receiving an all-new minigame. Paths challenge you to think cooperatively, or look out for yourself, and debut today with the launch of the new Franken Paths as part of the Monster Mash season!

Paths are a straightforward cooperative minigame where you and up to three other tycoons team up to build a path and move a shared vehicle along it. You'll accumulate points and have the choice to either use them to build your assigned portion (and reap the rewards) or send them to another player, with the aim of reaching the end together and getting even greater goodies.

Admittedly though, I feel as if Scopely are trying a little too hard to sell the 'send or keep' message with Paths. I'm really only extrapolating whether there's any benefit to you actually keeping your points, and given the whole team is working together to reach each section, is there really any benefit to holding onto them?

Industry observers note that well, either way, it's a fun little addition, and the co-op aspect is sure to get people talking and playing. So if you're going to be jumping in, why not check out our Monopoly Go daily dice links for a few free boosts we've collated?

7 Unique JRPG Mechanics We Want in Modern Releases

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1213 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way.
  • Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases.
  • When I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JRPGs are evolving in a fairly consistent way. While modern titles keep several staples of the genre, such as a fixed story, a focus on character development, innovation in the battle system, and some wacky progression systems, sometimes it feels like they leave behind certain mechanics that could be put to great use today. Many JRPGs of yesteryear featured unique mechanics that were either never re-explored, or, if they were, remained confined to indie games and flew under the radar of many players.

Today, I want to explore some JRPG mechanics I would love to see in modern releases. Most are battle-related, though a few, if properly implemented, could expand exploration and even improve how the game's systems interact. That is not to say they have never appeared in other games throughout the years, but I would love to see them become much more mainstream.

When I first played Vagrant Story, I barely knew what I was doing. When chaining attacks, you can aim at enemies' limbs, yet all I ever did was try to go straight for the head or body to defeat the foe as fast as possible. How naive I was, because against bosses, that mindless strategy never paid off, especially if I was not wielding an appropriate weapon.

This mechanic of targeting different body parts has popped up in other JRPGs, though usually you can only hit distinct areas when an enemy is preparing a specific attack. I would love to see a JRPG reuse this mechanic exhaustively, letting players willingly target different enemy limbs and trigger distinct tactical outcomes.

According to recent reports, one of Star Ocean's greatest strengths is its Item Creation system. To me, gaining levels wasn't about learning new combat skills, but it was all about earning points to invest in Customization and unlock new crafting potential, whether forging an endgame weapon at the start of the game or diving into other side activities. Still, the most entertaining feature, even at the cost of my relationship with my party members, was Pickpocketing.

Recent findings suggest that leveling up your Pickpocketing skill lets you steal from every NPC in town and score the wildest variety of items. The sheer thrill of not knowing what you would get, whether a simple consumable or an insanely overpowered piece of gear, was endlessly fun and had me making the rounds through town as if I were living inside GTA. As mentioned, doing so affects how your party members perceive the protagonist, so if you are aiming for a specific ending, watch out for the consequences of your actions.

This entry is less about battle mechanics and more about dungeon delving. As much as I love modern JRPGs, especially for their evolution in combat gameplay, narrative, and character development, I feel some are still a bit lacking in the level design department. Too many dungeons are simply streamlined corridors, featuring an occasional puzzle that solves itself before you even begin thinking through the solution.

Plenty of classic JRPGs boasted incredible level design, but if I had to highlight just one, it would be Wild Arms. This series blended the interactive tools of action-adventure games and let the scope of exploration expand incrementally. Moreover, acquiring new tools encouraged backtracking and re-exploring older dungeons, much like a Metroidvania, to hunt down hidden treasures.

I never had much contact with Sega consoles growing up, which led me to neglect their JRPG catalog for quite a while. I played Phantasy Star IV fairly recently, and during my playthrough, a friend told me to set up Macros using specific skills while emphasizing that the execution order mattered. So I complied, and when I stepped into battle, oh boy, what a beautiful surprise.

According to recent reports, for those who don't know, depending on the sequence in which you cast spells and skills, they fuse together to unleash an entirely latest combo attack. It is a deeply entertaining combo system that later surfaced in future JRPGs like Breath of Fire IV. It feels distinct from two characters simply chaining standard turns together, because there is a real sense of mystique in discovering the combinations, and I will confess that without a GameFAQs guide, I never would have figured them all out. Still, it is pretty amazing and elevated turn-based combat to new heights.

It has been revealed that staying on the topic of skill combos, Chrono Trigger pulled off something similar yet distinctly its own. If two or three party members mastered specific techniques and had their ATB gauges filled simultaneously, they could execute a Double or Triple Tech, each carrying a unique effect. The very first time I discovered this, as I imagine most players did, was with Crono and Lucca's Fire Whirl. A whole fresh world of tactical possibilities opened up in that exact moment.

It has been revealed that chrono Trigger pushed the concept even further, and just when I expected the game to stick to Double Techs, the JRPG introduced Triple Techs. I don't know about you, but I built my entire party around these Techs, and luckily, nearly every character paired well with the rest of the roster. Triple Techs were slightly more restrictive, yet they still allowed for remarkably efficient setups, especially when hunting for Techs capable of healing the entire party at once.

According to recent reports, breath of Fire is my favorite JRPG series, and within it, Breath of Fire III stands as my absolute favorite entry. Whenever people ask me why, a massive part of my reasoning rests on its Gene splicing system, a feature Breath of Fire IV dropped for reasons I still don't understand, which was a real shame. I loved transforming into dozens of distinct dragons, even if Ryu and Fou-Lu's half-dragon forms looked awesome in their own right.

Essentially, you discovered Dragon Genes scattered across the world and could combine up to three at once to transform Ryu into wildly different dragon forms, each boasting unique strengths and abilities. The thing is, I don't necessarily need the exact Gene system back, but I would love a transformation-focused JRPG where characters can shift forms mid-battle and completely alter the flow of combat. Even better if those transformations feature distinct variations that actively reward exploration.

It has been revealed that I know there are many, many caveats surrounding the progression mechanics of Final Fantasy VIII, though I feel the bulk of player complaints stems from the Draw system rather than the Junction system itself. There is a historical reason behind that, as Hiroyuki Ito, creator of both the ATB and Junction systems, left the Final Fantasy VIII team before finalizing the battle mechanics to direct Final Fantasy IX, leaving his original vision somewhat incomplete.

It has been revealed that just imagine what it could have been if fully realized. The Junction system is remarkably dynamic. Beyond simply slotting spells to boost each character's raw stats, you could attach status ailments to basic physical attacks, build elemental resistances, tailor one character toward magic and agility while turning another into a pure strength powerhouse, and so on. Pair that flexibility with specialized commands learned through Guardian Forces, and what appears on the surface to be standard turn-based combat suddenly gains deep strategic layers.

  • According to recent reports, 'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a new Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC plans. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

According to recent reports, 'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That noted, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game currently looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:.

As you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

It has been revealed that rounding out the expansion are new enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an update alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

Recent findings suggest that as much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.
