💡 Key Takeaways
  • CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion.
  • According to recent reports, game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted".
  • It has been revealed that after a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. The move's been made with the permission of Geralt's Polish voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, and is rooted in the studio wanting his latest lines to sound similar to the ones he recorded for the original game prior to having a stroke which has altered how he sounds.

According to recent reports, game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted". With next year's Songs of the Past expansion, CD Projekt Red were seemingly more concerned about making sure lines recorded by post-stroke Rozenek don't sound markedly different to those he recorded a decade ago for the base game and its existing expansions.

It has been revealed that after a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings. Rozenek reportedly gave his blessing for this to go ahead. "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," he told Game File. "I have great trust...for the creators of this game.".

Sources indicate that this isn't the first time CD Projekt Red have enlisted Respeecher's services. Back in 2023, it was revealed that the studio had used speech synthesis software to make ripperdoc Viktor Vektor's lines in the Polish version of Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion sound like actor Miłogost Reczek. Reczek died in 2021 before he could reprise his role as Vektor for the DLC, so rather than recasting the character across the whole game to avoid noticeable differences in voice, CD Projekt got another actor to voice Vektor's latest lines for Phantom Liberty, then used the genAI tech to make those lines sound like Reczek was delivering them. CD Projekt Red said at the time that they'd gotten permission from Reczek's family before going ahead with their plan.

Speaking to Game File about this latest use of genAI on Rozenek's Songs of the Past lines, CD Projekt localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed noted that "as a person working with voice actors over all the regions in the world, this is a big concern". "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good," he added. The argument the studio are making at current is that this was "a special case" due to Rozenek's specific situation with Songs of the Past.

Geralt's English voice actor Doug Cockle reportedly won't have his lines for the upcoming expansion get the same genAI treatment, nor will any lines Rozenek records for future Witcher games, with the studio seemingly happy to lean on the passage of in-game time as an explanation for Geralt sounding different in the latter case.

According to recent reports, as ever, there's a debate to be had as to whether CD Projekt Red should have simply recast Rozenek's role in Songs of the Past if the difference bothered them so, possibly while bringing the actor on to help tutor whomever his human replacement for Songs of the Past would be in nailing the exact gravelly tone needed for Geralt. That way, you'd have two actors being paid for work rather than forking out for genAI instead of one of them, though it's possibly an idea that'd only work well in theory. If I were Rozenek I'm not sure I'd be totally happy aiding someone who could potentially be tapped to replace me going forwards, though it does very much seem like the lesser of two evils when compared to the potential of voice actors being replaced by genAI line readings.

It has been revealed that as far as the game alone is concerned, I'm also not sure Geralt's voice being different in the upcoming expansion is something that'd bother me too much when playing. One would assume he'd not suddenly be sounding like a member of Alvin and the Chipmunks, and there are plenty of storyline justifications you could concoct or lean on for him sounding that bit gruffer at times.

Recent findings suggest that let's start with the basics. Redmagic 12 Pro specs I won't go into every single detail, but as a gamer, these are the most crucial ones you need to take into consideration:.

Industry observers note that if you are someone who isn’t heavily into technology, the description of the specs above might not mean all that much to you. However, believe me, we are talking about cutting-edge technology when it comes to the mobile gaming phone market. In simple words, it's far ahead of its time.

Describing this specific model simply as a mobile phone is probably a mistake, since we're essentially talking about the equivalent of a top-tier gaming console that can run any game on max settings without lag or frame drops.

Better display and... The phone features a 6.85-inch screen with 5,000 nits peak brightness and a 185 Hz refresh rate. The screen is surrounded by super-thin bezels (less than 1 mm), giving it a 96.3% screen-to-body ratio. It uses a 9th-generation 16-megapixel selfie camera hidden invisibly beneath the wall-to-wall display. Improved... cameras!? Since the front camera is virtually invisible when casually using the phone or gaming, this gives it an edge. Oh, and I have to admit, there have been some tweaks to the back cameras - I can't quite pinpoint it, but the software has been upgraded, improving the photo quality.

According to recent reports, I've been slightly disappointed by the cameras of some of the previous models, which I've clearly voiced in my reviews. In this case... I really don't have much to complain about. That came as a surprise, but a really good one! Hop on the cooling system hype train! The Redmagic 12 Pro uses the Aqua Core Cooling System 3.0, which is a hybrid cooling system that combines air and dual cooling loops with anti-freezing coolant. That's just something you don't see every day.

It has been revealed that in terms of gaming, that means the phone is capable of withstanding temperatures from -60°C up to 108°C. To give you a point of reference, if you are a user of the previous version, this one is 85% better. The fan runs at 25,500 RPM and pushes air toward the vents. You can even feel the air being pushed out if you hold your finger next to the fan.

Recent findings suggest that unsurprisingly, the battery lasts forever The massive 8,400 mAh battery (which supports both fast wired charging and wireless charging) lets you keep gaming or watching videos for hours upon hours. The software automatically adjusts the cooling system to keep the battery from overheating, so you will never have to worry about it.

If my math is correct, if the phone remains idle, battery life sits somewhere between 230 and 240 hours. Basically, it can last around 10 days. Redmagic 12 Pro was created for gaming, but let's be honest - it's good for everything Based on everything up to this point, you can probably tell that this gem is aimed primarily at gamers. Of course, that doesn't have to mean it cannot also be used as an everyday phone, just like any other. Quite the opposite, in fact - I believe it can meet all the daily needs you might need from your phone, and elevate the experience.

In a recent development, the downside (if you can even call it that) is that doing so would be like buying a track-ready racecar, just to go to the supermarket. I mean, you don't really need the best phone on the market just to play Solitaire and other Facebook games. Can it be done? Certainly. Is it something I would recommend to a friend? Probably not.

I mean, you even get a PC emulator, which works wonders if you connect it to your Steam account and want to play some titles from your library on the go. While this feature is still in Beta, I have to admit, it worked well and it was a nice touch. The new small improvements bring massive QOL changes! Admittedly, one thing I didn’t wasn't too excited about when it came to the previous versions of Redmagic phones was the case. Recent findings suggest that well, one of the very first things I noticed when I got my hands on the Redmagic 12 Pro was that its design has changed slightly. I know this might sound a bit funny to some people, but when you interact with something every single day, you truly realise that sometimes the small details make all the difference. And let’s be honest - nobody wants to drop a phone of this value down the stairs (yet it is something that can happen).

Speaking of its durability, I would like to mention that the screen is covered by Gorilla Glass 7i. What that means is that coins, keys, and other items you might have in your pocket or bag won't scratch it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

Sources indicate that the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

According to recent reports, marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

Sources indicate that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Upcoming Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

Sources indicate that this isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-new globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Sources indicate that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no confirmed platforms.

Recent findings suggest that although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

In a recent development, this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

According to recent reports, of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

There are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

Critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

Sources indicate that until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. There are so, so many details to uncover all over the place if you take a moment to stop and look for them, and I’m not just talking about Bigfoot hanging out in the swamps or the many varieties of bird flying around. There are lots of little details that subtly inform aspects of the characters’ personalities and interests, including, apparently, the particular brands of power tools they prefer.

Industry observers note that A certain subset of players couldn’t help but notice that the tools Jason uses when fixing the walls and roof are colored a distinct shade of yellow. The brand printed on the tool may be different from real-life, but fans of hardware know the distinct iconography of DeWalt when they see it.

According to recent reports, for those with no interest in power tools, DeWalt is one of the most prominent brands in the scene, manufacturing all of the usual implements like power drills, nail guns, circular saws, and all that other good stuff, usually powered by rechargeable battery packs. As is so often the case with this sort of thing, fans of DeWalt have something of an unofficial rivalry with fans of other major hardware brands, especially Milwaukee, whose tools are usually colored red.

Recent findings suggest that during Jason’s various household repair chores, he uses a couple of power tools colored the same shade of yellow as DeWalt’s, both emblazoned with the logo “DEVICE.” Obviously, Rockstar can’t just use DeWalt’s actual logo in its game without its permission (though I have a feeling DeWalt would’ve loved it if given the opportunity), but the particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable. Looks like Jason is a DeWalt man, and fans on the DeWalt subreddit are holding this up as a victory over the likes of Milwaukee.

The particular font that the “DEVICE” logo is printed in, particularly with the slightly smaller “E” before the “V,” is unmistakable.

According to recent reports, the particular implements that Jason uses seem to be at least partially inspired by real-life DeWalt tools. The driver he uses when fixing the walls is nearly identical to DeWalt’s 20V MAX 1/4 inch impact driver. The nail gun he uses to fix the fencing and roof doesn’t seem to have as close of a parallel, but it most closely-resembles the DeWalt 20V MAX XR brad nailer. That’s not a roofing-specific nailer, though, so either I’m wrong or Jason just doesn’t differentiate between nailer types. I’d believe either scenario.

While this may seem like a granular detail to hyperfixate on, as I mentioned, it’s just kind of fun to examine every aspect of this simulated world. In addition to what I noted before about a character’s hardware preferences, it’s also interesting to hold up these simulated knock-off brands next to the real world.

Sources indicate that A significant part of the long-established aesthetic of the GTA world is riffing on aspects of real life. It’s always been a very exaggerated setting, often exemplifying the absolute worst parts of modern society for both laughs and drama. The fictional state of Leonida is pretty much Florida if it was slightly worse, and the same goes for Vice City and Miami.

GTA has also parodied more than its fair share of real-life brands and corporations over its various entries, usually with much sillier, ruder names. Sprite becomes “Sprunk,” IKEA becomes “KRAPEA,” and Twitter becomes “Bleeter,” which I am sincerely happy did not change its name to “Blex” or something equally stupid since GTA 5.

We interrupt your Grand Theft Auto 6 playtime to bring you the following announcement: there are more games launching today.

Yes, while 19th November 2026 will forever be known as 'GTA 6 Day ', a handful of other games are also braving the launch window and are releasing on Switch today.

We know that your adventures in Leonida will take priority, and that's okay, but we thought it was only right to highlight the other experiences that didn't back down from the substantial boy's launch aims. And no, we're not highlighting everything launching on Switch today, since, well, the eShop is always bombarded with questionable titles that probably aren't worth checking out.

If, however, you're on the hunt for something with fewer Vice City vibes, here are some other options launching today.

There's every chance that you have already played through Bedtime Digital's Figment and Figment 2: Creed Valley when they introduced on Switch 1 a few years back, but the Switch 2 versions are also launching today with some neat performance bumps. We're talking 60fps at 1080p and "enhanced graphics". Sounds ripe for a replay, if you ask us.

Published and developed by room6, this is a roguelike all about gathering cute pixel art plushies to your aid and using their powers to survive a nighttime onslaught of monsters. Need we say more? It seems to strike that balance of cute/creepy pretty well, and we can see it being quite the time sink, with 40 recruitable plushies, 100 items and 20 costumes available to mix up every run.

It has been revealed that those who frequent Japanese merch stalls will no doubt recognise the Sumikkogurashi gang. This one sees the team of adorable little blobs tasked with helping out at onsen inns to ensure their smooth running. There's plenty of minigames and scope to expand the inns further, but come on, the cuteness is the major draw here. Just look at those little guys!

It's The Binding of Isaac again (again). This re-release features all of the game's DLC content and the chance to play it with up to four players online.

Desperate for more throwback shooting after breezing through Boltgun? Auroch Digital has got you covered. After launching on other consoles last month, Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun 2 finally arrives on Switch 2 today with even more strafing, shooting and scary monstrosities. The score features a surprise cameo track from composer Mick Gordon (DOOM, DOOM Eternal, Wolfenstein: The Newly introduced Order), which is an added bonus for music fans.

Naturally, the eShop will be home to many more debuts today, but the above selection gives a pretty good range of options (and a certain quality that a bunch of the other releases lack). Let us know in the comments if there's another newbie today that we've missed!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
  • Sources indicate that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

Sources indicate that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the massive fresh world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

According to recent reports, the squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

According to recent reports, as you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two upcoming 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

It has been revealed that general Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

It has been revealed that her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

Sources indicate that the other new arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Recent findings suggest that version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

Sources indicate that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the newly introduced outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

It has been revealed that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be announced at a later date.

#29179. Latest Update: Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2109 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2109 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while.
  • Instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news.
  • Also bear in mind we've had a fair old bit of inflation in recent years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while. But I come back to you now at the turn of the technological tide. Well, sort of. Sadly I'm not here to predict an end to the ridiculous AI-fuelled chip crisis. That whole mess has a couple of years to run, surely.

Instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news. In short, have you seen how cheap PC gaming monitors are? I mean remarkably, almost stupendously, cheap. I'm talking £60 / $60 for an entry-level 1080p panel with triple-digit refresh rate, sub-£200 / $250 for high-refresh 4K gaming. Heck, even OLED monitors now start with a "2" in both currencies.

Also bear in mind we've had a fair old bit of inflation in recent years. A 4K panel bought today for £200 is equivalent to paying roughly £150 back in 2020. All the while, that same £200 / $200 right now won't buy you a current-model gaming graphics card at all, even the most feeble example, and will barely secure a basic dual-channel 16GB DDR5 memory kit. Youch.

In a recent development, so, I think we can all agree monitors are cheap in the current chip-catastrophe context. The immediate question is why? The answer isn't all that complicated, actually. Most obviously, the display market isn't being devoured by the AI craze. All those data centres are stuffed with GPUs, memory chips and NAND flash, not monitors.

By way of example, one of the largest new AI data centres on Earth is Microsoft's new Fairwater site in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin. It's thought to pack hundreds of thousands of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs. The cost doesn't bear thinking about, but those GPUs are built into what's known as "headless" server racks. In other words, they have no screens at all. Ultimately, the key compute hardware is all managed remotely, in which capacity the Fairwater facility is reported to right now have around 375 employees. If we generously assume each has two PC monitors, that's only 750 for the entire site.

AI isn't really driving demand on the end-user side of the equation, either. Put it this way: you don't need to buy a new phone, laptop or PC to access the latest models. At the same time, the display market is suffering from something of a glut of overcapacity. Chinese companies built out huge capacity in LCD panel manufacturing over the past decade, to the extent factories are now running underutilised. Meanwhile, even the OLED market is arguably oversupplied.

It has been revealed that in fact, Samsung and LG, the two substantial noises in large OLED panel manufacturing (as opposed to OLED displays for tablets and phones), have been shifting emphasis away from TV panels to PC monitors because the latter offer better margins. Meanwhile, the AI boom has almost definitely meant lower demand for upcoming PCs. Certainly, the big research houses point to cratering PC sales thanks to higher component costs. Long story short, that's oodles of capacity combined with weakening demand. Like I remarked, the explanation for cheap monitors isn't exactly rocket surgery, if you know what I mean.

It has been revealed that what is a bit more complicated is making sense of what's available today in the gaming monitor market. With so much choice, where exactly is the very best value to be found? And are there any remaining pain points?

It has been revealed that monitor specifications, to be sure, can be tricksy at the best of times. But if you're looking for some blanket rules to fling casually over the whole LCD monitor market - I'll be digging deeper into OLED tech another day - try these for size. Look for, at minimum, 300 nits brightness and 1ms response times. Refresh rates are a slightly more complicated call, but for the vast majority of games, 144Hz is plenty. For "esports-grade multiplayer fare like Counter-Strike or Dota 2, or I think a refresh in the high 200s will get the job done for most. If you'll benefit from more than that, you almost certainly know who you are already.

Oh, and heavily favour IPS over VA panels. Exceptions exist: there are some decent "Rapid VA" panels these days and Samsung, in particular, does some nippy VA models. But a lot of the cheaper stuff is pretty slow and smeary, making VA a risky buy. Finally, don't worry too much about claimed HDR capability, save for the fact that HDR 400 certification at least means the monitor can do 400 nits. Unless a monitor has local dimming, it won't be truly HDR capable.

Sources indicate that anywho, one immediate and rather ironic glitch is the growing mismatch between monitors and GPUs. For sure, it's great you can grab a high-refresh 4K monitor for such little money. It's almost hard to believe that you can have this 27-inch IPS MSI for sub-£200 (you're looking at $250 for the same model in the US), and it even has a 288Hz 1080p dual mode.

I actually favour 32 inches with my 4K gaming, and that's naturally a little pricier, especially if you insist on an IPS - which again, you probably should. But even $350 for that kind of panel (here's a comparable model for £340 in the UK) is a fraction of what you'd have paid for a similarly specced model a few years ago. And it probably wouldn't have included dual-mode functionality.

Here's the problem, though. How are you going to drive the thing, what with its eight million-plus pixels? After all, the cheapest RTX 5090 on Newegg right now is over $6,500. So high-end Nvidia GPUs now cost about as much as a decent used car.

Sources indicate that of course, you might be surprised just how effective the likes of an AMD RX 9070 XT or Nvidia RTX 5070-class GPU is at 4K thanks to upscaling technologies including DLSS and FSR. The latest transformer model upscalers really do knock out pretty stellar image quality. Add in a bit of frame gen and you have a compelling combination of visual sharpness, reasonably low latency and nice smoothframe rates, even in the most demanding of games. Perhaps the one thing you can't do is enable full path tracing in a game like Cyberpunk 2077 and still expect a slick experience, but standard ray tracing remains an option.

In a recent development, the bigger snag, unsurprisingly, is that you can no longer bag a 5070 at (let alone below) its original £539 / $549 MSRP. Instead, you're looking at the thick end of £800 / $900. That's a bit of an ask for pairing with a £200 monitor, isn't it?

Industry observers note that I'd therefore argue that, for pure gaming purposes, the bang-for-buck sweet spot remains just where it's been sat twiddling its thumbs for the better part of a decade, namely 1440p. That applies to both its vanilla 16:9 aspect variety and my personally preferred ultrawide format, the latter being so very immersive and also pretty nifty for daily multi-tasking. Indeed, the 27-inch 1440p segment even brings the vibrant colours and infinite contrast of OLED panels into a reasonably affordable window.

It has been revealed that by way of example, £179 (or $150) is enough for a circa 200Hz, IPS 1440p panel with super low (by IPS standards) pixel response, even if the 250-nit brightness is lower than I'd like. Meanwhile, as I write these words, pricing for substantial-brand 27-inch 1440p gaming OLEDs kicks off at about £290 in the UK and roughly $270 in the US. Admittedly, those entry-level OLEDs come with some compromises, which I'll cover in a forthcoming post. But what you might call 'proper' OLED panels can be had around the low £300 / $300 mark - not throw-away money, for sure, but relatively accessible.

Industry observers note that the 34-inch 1440p ultrawide segment is a bit trickier, however. The good news is that conventional LCD models can be had for relative peanuts, with prices starting at about £220 or $249 for game-focused, high-refresh models. But those two example both use a VA panel, which usually means inferior pixel response.

IPS models are a little thin on the ground when it comes to 34-inch ultrawide, but sneaking in below £300 / $300 is generally possible. The real bummer is OLED, where going ultrawide invokes a massive premium. The best price I can find on a big-brand 34-inch ultrawide today is $629 for this Asus model in the US and £648 for this MSI option in the UK.

That's awfully toppy, especially when you consider that you can grab a 49-inch, 5,120x1,440 ultrawide OLED for barely any more money. I do actually quite like those 49-inch ultrawides, but I have to concede the ergonomics are challenging. However, 4K OLEDs in 27-inch and 32-inch formats can also be had for as much as £100 / $100 less than the current cheapest 34-inch 1440p ultrawides, which doesn't make much sense to me.

Recent findings suggest that again, with 4K, there's the challenge of keeping all those pixels updated. If you already have a sufficiently mighty graphics card, though, I a 32-inch 4K OLED can make a fantastic all-round option, and something like this MSI model for £549 would be absolutely lovely. You get good pixel density and lots of space for daily desktopping, plus OLED visuals and a large enough panel to be really get you into your games.

It's just a pity that 34-inch OLED ultrawides remain so weirdly expensive, it being a format that ticks so many different boxes. As for my own personal money-no-object pick, well, I'm typing these words on the new Alienware AW3926QW, the 39-inch 5K2K beast with a Tandem WOLED panel and RGB subpixels.

According to recent reports, one could argue it's a relative steal at £1,079 or $1,100. I mean, it's pretty much peak current PC gaming display technology, and it's about half the price of what Nvidia's second-tier RTX 5080 graphics card is going for lately. Assuming you can even find one in stock.

In a recent development, at this point, the one major category I haven't covered is LCD monitors with mini-LED full-array local dimming. Cards on the table, I'm not a huge fan of mini-LED monitors. The detailed reasons for that are, perhaps, the subject for another day. But I've reviewed countless models and have yet to see one that didn't come with pretty serious compromises.

In a recent development, that noted, the technology has gotten a lot more accessible in the last 12 to 18 months, to the extent that 27-inch 1440p models start at just over $250. I've had that specific model in and came away pretty impressed. It's very, very punchy, and even factoring in the limitations of mini-LED versus OLED when it comes to lighting control and speed, I cannot deny the temptation.

It has been revealed that just for completeness, one further exception to the general rule of cheap gaming monitors involves ultra-high refresh monitors aimed at serious esports aficionados. I'm talking about panels like this 1,000Hz LG I sampled elsewhere. At £800 / $1,000 for a 25-inch 1080p IPS panel it's inevitably a niche proposition, and poor value by normal standards.

In a recent development, I think a much better compromise for just about everyone, short of an actual esports pro, is to grab a larger, higher resolution monitor that offers one of those windowed 1080p modes running at about 500Hz or thereabouts. That way you've got a nice high-res panel for both work and play, as well as that ultra-low latency mode for when you want to dance around Dust 2 doling out the headshots or whatever.

Incidentally, I realise I've gone in a bit hot and heavy with the OLED content here, the implicit assumption being OLED is all that, and notably without addressing the obvious objections like the risk of burn-in. But all that, I hope you'll be pleased to hear, is very much the subject for my next RPS post on all things OLED.

According to recent reports, until then, all I can say is thank goodness PC monitors provide relative respite from the parlous state of much of the rest of the PC component market. It's absolutely brutal out there if you're building a gaming PC, but at least you'll get a lot of screen for your money.

Just to round things out, if anyone has any specific queries at any given price point, form factor or panel type, shout out below and I'll try to steer you in the direction of a decent model.

After Bethesda formally named The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel earlier this month, some series fans were hopeful that more news wasn't far behind. Skyrim is 15 years old today (11th November) after all, but Bethesda Game Studios has since dashed those hopes into oblivion.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

"Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any massive announcements tomorrow," the social media account wrote. "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything fresh on Sentinel for some time.".

Industry observers note that the Elder Scrolls fans have already been waiting for the series' next mainline follow-up for, erm, also quite some time. Specifically, Skyrim came out in 2011, The Elder Scrolls 6's first reveal trailer reared its head in 2018, and BGS' Starfield took to the stars in 2023 - a wait so long that it had even the most faithful among us questioning if a new Elder Scrolls could ever recapture the series' magic.

So, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

In the meantime, Bethesda isn't letting Skyrim's 15th anniversary go by without a few celebrations. For one, the seminal role-playing game is deeply discounted on all platforms, in the very unlikely scenario you haven't tried it out yet.

The Elder Scrolls Online Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim is also joining the festivities by adding the Greymoor Chapter into the base game for free, giving everyone access to a few famous Skyrim locales and more. Sources indicate that there are plenty of controversial game franchises out there. But many are pretty lazy, and either intentionally racist, sexist or simply provocative. A truly controversial series is one that sets out to do something, and does so in an unapologetic and probably disturbing way. In unrelated news, Running With Scissors' Postal Classic & Uncut is out now on Google Play!

Unlike, say, Postal II, there's no wackiness or crass humour here. The story is simple: You are the Dude, and everybody else has to die. That means blasting your way through dozens of levels ranging from suburban neighbourhoods to downtown metropolises, with a variety of firearms and explosives, as you face down police officers, armed residents and plenty of unarmed civilians caught in the crossfire.

In a recent development, the Earth is Hungry Postal is a series that, while I won't necessarily defend, I think everyone will agree has an undercurrent of potential. The original Postal veers between exciting and chilling, as each level is interspersed with the paranoid ramblings of the Dude. And while the official story may be that you're defending yourself against crazed gunmen, all those people running for their lives may beg to differ.

Industry observers note that in other words, you're stepping into the disturbed mind of a crazed gunman. Not hard to see why this was so controversial back in the day.

According to recent reports, it's a thoroughly dark, brooding and unnerving concept, and one that Running With Scissors are revisiting in the upcoming Flesh & Wire, a more horror-focused FPS set in the aftermath of the Dude's rampage. Of course, if you strip all that away, Postal remains a pretty solid isometric shooter and a real 90s snapshot.

If you've got a strong stomach for it, you can find Postal Classic & Uncut available on Android, with all 16 original levels and four from the Special Delivery expansion included.

Industry observers note that postal Classic & Uncut is definitely not a cheery game for the weekend. So if you need something a little calmer and more laid-back, why not check out our latest list of the five fresh mobile games to try this week?

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

In a recent development, the ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

It has been revealed that the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Sources indicate that heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group.

The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

"Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler mentioned in a press release.

It has been revealed that black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the manufacturer swallowed up countless big names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024.

According to recent reports, it doesn't sound like Black Forest split with the rights to the Destroy All Humans series or its permanently mean alien protag Crypto, but the studio has mentioned it's still working with THQ Nordic in some capacity. The original Destroy All Humans run nosedived wildly in quality after the second game, so I'm not sure how exciting a remake of, let's say, Destroy All Humans: Massive Willy Unleashed would be nowadays, though I'd definitely be interested in seeing Crypto again in another ridiculously silly, sometimes rude and anarchic adventure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since its release earlier this year, Hell Let Loose: Vietnam has gotten plenty of praise for capturing the grit and horrors of the jungles of Vietnam. At the same time, the game has also been on the receiving end of criticism for its rather limited arsenal.

Industry observers note that the dev team over at Expression Games has taken that to heart. After addressing the two more glaring omissions by adding the American M14 and the Soviet SKS, the most iconic Western weapon of the Cold War is finally making its way to Southeast Asia.

The next major release for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, patch 2.0, is bringing the FN FAL into the fray, specifically in its British version that saw combat in the region.

Introduced in 1953, the FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

According to recent reports, chambered for the same 7.62x51mm NATO as the M14, M40 and M60 already in the game, the L1A1 SLR (Self-Loading Rifle) variant comes with a 20-round box magazine and is limited to semi-automatic fire. This was a design choice by Commonwealth clients, and really, unless you want to shoot down NVA planes while aiming at the horizon, you won’t notice the difference.

According to recent reports, in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, the L1A1 will be available to the United States & Allies faction to represent its service with Australian and Latest Zealander units deployed there. Unlike the M14, the new rifle won’t be available to the Rifleman role.

The FAL holds the distinction of being the first modern service rifle to enter widespread service in the West.

To use the L1A1, you’ll need to reach level 6 in one of the following roles:.

I want to caveat here that if you actually pick the L1A1 over the M60 while playing machine gunner, you are a bad person and your team will be short in firepower. MG roles are for pouring it on downrange, not for reloading after twenty shots, and I’m saying this as a staunch FAL defender.

The developers have not offered any insight on how the pilots are supposed to fit a rifle that long in the cockpit of the Huey, but we can look the other way for a little bit.

As much as I’m pining for the L1A1 and it will be my personal highlight of patch 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, it’s hard to argue against the real big item on the prospective patch notes being the Khe Sanh map and what it means for the game as a whole.

Khe Sanh will be the debut map for the Assault game mode, doubling down on the attackers versus defenders gameplay already present in the Offensive mode.

Industry observers note that assault brings back a fan favorite from the World War 2 Hell Let Loose, and focuses specifically on horrific trench warfare, strongpoints, and choosing whether you prefer dying in a fatal funnel in a trench or getting ripped apart by artillery out in the open. It’s great fun once you get used to the tinnitus.

Level designer Kienan Suthar provides more detail in this deep dive:.

The battle of Khe Sanh was one of the toughest battles in the Vietnam War, coinciding with the Tet Offensive of January 1968 and lasting until July of that same year.

Khe Sanh Combat Base was surrounded by a large North Vietnamese force, supported by Viet Cong and Pathet Lao rebels. For five months, US and allied forces reinforced the base primarily from the air, while throwing everything and the kitchen sink at the Vietnamese troops.

It has been revealed that the outcome of the battle, as many major engagements of the Vietnam War, was inconclusive. The North Vietnamese siege was partially lifted by April 1968, but a shift in US strategy in the aftermath of the Tet Offensive led to its abandonment on July 9.

For the Americans, avoiding a Điện Biên Phủ situation and preventing the collapse of the base was considered a win. The North Vietnamese, meanwhile, celebrated victory by capturing the region following the withdrawal.

For players, the real tangible outcome is that it created an incredibly dense network of fortifications for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam to sink its teeth into the assault mode.

It has been revealed that update 2.0 for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is scheduled for the first half of December. Hell Let Loose: Vietnam is right now available on PC, PlayStation 5, and XBOX Series X/S.

Feature: 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.
  • The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be mentioned for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.
  • It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.

The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be mentioned for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.

It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.

If you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere. Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.

Ready? Let's dive right into things...

Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.

Batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.

Industry observers note that steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones-style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.

However, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.

A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party, followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.

Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.

Sources indicate that this one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

One of the few games Europeans got which never saw the light of day in North America, Disaster: Day of Crisis is a Monolith Soft joint that showcases the Wiimote's versatility with different control schemes across its four main gameplay styles, which naturally includes those video game staples, shooting and driving.

The latter is handled with the Remote held horizontally, while outside the Nunchuk-controlled walking sections, the game becomes a pointer-based rail shooter.

According to recent reports, with a blockbusting story that crams in volcanoes alongside shady outfits and plenty of (melo)drama, it doesn't quite cohere as it should, and there are certainly better-looking titles on the system. But as a curio from a studio with an enviable pedigree — and a game that apparently didn't pass Reggie Fils-Aimé's quality bar for release — it's a fascinating glimpse at Monolith's Wii-era thinking before Xenoblade Chronicles dropped two years later.

Excite Truck was an underrated gem in the Wii's early life, with satisfying motion controls that paired beautifully with the wallow-y physics of the arcade monster trucks you raced.

In a recent development, it also let you load up MP3s on your SD card and make your own soundtrack, which felt like a bit of magic to some Wii gamers (read: this Wii gamer) back in 2006. Nothing like boosting over a canyon with Gwen Stefani booming through the speakers. Good times.

According to recent reports, having recently fired up Excite Truck, I can confirm that this holds up beautifully, with subtle controls and a suitable sense of heft and face-blasting speed. Helluva game.

It has been revealed that excitebots, Monster Games' 2009 follow-up, kept the arcade sensibilities and challenging terrain but switched out the trucks for on-wheel robots. It's a fantastic game that injects a little more personality into the basic structure of Excite Truck while keeping the speed and excitement.

Sources indicate that sadly, it's also a game which never launched in Europe, so we're at the moment tit-for-tat after Disaster: Day of Crisis. North America got the better deal, there.

Look, it's an inconsequential Zelda spin-off designed to showcase the Wii Zapper, but it is a system-exclusive inconsequential Zelda spin-off. Can you afford not to have it in your collection?

Hmm, probably. There's a reason this target-practice game is bottom of our Zelda list. Still, it's not unenjoyable, still dirt cheap, and it's got Twilight Princess-era Link on the box. I've somehow ended up with two copies. One of those 'oh, I don't have this' moments when you get home and realise 'yes, I already have this.'.

Another 'built for Wii' game that came to other platforms later (Vita in 2012, PC in 2016), Cing's Little King's Story added dashes of Doshin The Giant and Pikmin to a real-time strategy tale of the titular diminutive king working to expand the reach of his kingdom one citizen at a time and conquer neighbouring territories,.

An engaging genre mash-up that holds its own alongside the previously mentioned Pikmin series while putting a fresh spin on things, this was one of the last games Cing (Hotel Dusk, Another Code) released. Two years later, the firm filed for bankruptcy.

When PlatinumGames' name is on the box, you expect style - and MadWorld certainly delivered that with its inky, Sin City-esque aesthetic that splattered blood red across a black-and-white canvas.

At a time when all the serious games elsewhere were shiny and brown and grey, this Sega-published chainsaw-'em-up also helped demonstrate that Wii wasn't only a console for fluffy technicolour worlds and cuddly mascots.

As a hack-and-slash brawler, it's not up there with the developer's finest work - there's definitely an element of style over substance here. But when the style is this good, it's still worth the space on the shelf.

Honestly, at this point we all thought we'd have access to this on Switch one way or another — via NSO if not a proper remaster. However, at the time of writing (and discounting the now-unavailable Wii U eShop release of the Trilogy), this Metroid is still a Wii exclusive.

We can only assume it will arrive at some point — Nintendo now has the four Pikmin games on Switch, so it's about time to plug the Prime gap, too.

And staying on that theme, let's stick with Samus over the page...

It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

According to recent reports, nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. It has been revealed that that’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

10 Games to Play If You Loved Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1862 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there are few things worse than finishing a fantastic adventure and realizing you have no idea what to play next.
  • After spending hours exploring Hyrule, solving puzzles, and facing some of gaming's most memorable bosses, it's only natural to feel a little lost when the credits finally roll.
  • While no game can truly replace the feeling of playing Ocarina of Time for the first time, there are plenty of experiences out there that capture some of the same magic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are few things worse than finishing a fantastic adventure and realizing you have no idea what to play next. With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake arriving earlier this month, plenty of players are probably reaching that bittersweet moment already!

After spending hours exploring Hyrule, solving puzzles, and facing some of gaming's most memorable bosses, it's only natural to feel a little lost when the credits finally roll. But don't worry, because I'm here to help you find your next adventure.

While no game can truly replace the feeling of playing Ocarina of Time for the first time, there are plenty of experiences out there that capture some of the same magic. Whether it's a mysterious world waiting to be explored, clever dungeons, unforgettable characters, or a story that stays with you long after you've put the controller down, there's something on this list for every kind of Zelda fan.

So, if you're already missing Hyrule and aren't quite ready to say goodbye to that feeling of adventure, here are 10 games worth checking out. Some might remind you of classic Zelda, while others take those familiar ideas in completely different directions. Either way, I think you'll find something worth getting lost in!

In a recent development, nothing beats dealing with the sadness of finishing a fantastic game by jumping straight into its sequel, right? That's why we're kicking things off with Majora's Mask, the final Zelda entry released on the Nintendo 64 and one of the darkest adventures in the entire franchise.

According to recent reports, although it reuses plenty of assets and the basic gameplay of Ocarina of Time, Majora's has an entirely different atmosphere. There's no Triforce, no Princess Zelda to rescue, and no Ganondorf plotting to take over Hyrule. Instead, a mysterious moon is about to crash into the town of Termina, and Link happens to have his Ocarina stolen by the mischievous creature responsible for the whole mess – then, well, someone has to save the day!

This leads to one of the most fascinating mechanics in the series: a three-day time loop that has you traveling through time, helping eccentric characters, and learning the daily schedules of the town's residents. Interestingly, the Ocarina of Time remake actually brings a little more of that NPC schedule system into its own villages, making this sequel feel like a particularly natural follow-up.

If you love the combination of dungeons, memorable boss fights, unusual mechanics, and, of course, a lovely talking companion, then Okami should be right up your alley.

Recent findings suggest that with a structure heavily inspired by classic Zelda adventures, this is one of Capcom's most beloved games, and its story draws heavily from Japanese folklore, following Amaterasu, the sun goddess who takes the form of a white wolf. She must restore life to a land plagued by an ancient evil, beginning with a legendary eight-headed demon that was sealed away a hundred years earlier. Gods, broken seals, spirits, and a spreading darkness? Yeah, I think that should ring a bell for anyone familiar with Hyrule.

It's a perfect pick if you're craving another Zelda-like adventure, and the upcoming sequel gives you one more reason to fall in love with this world.

Recent findings suggest that mina the Hollower takes place in a world filled with talking skeletons and every kind of magical fantasy you can imagine. So, if the Ocarina of Time left you craving another adventure packed with charming characters and a wonderfully imaginative world, this little indie game might be exactly what you're looking for.

This is a 2D action-adventure with roots deeply tied to some of the most iconic games in the genre – and yes, The Legend of Zelda is definitely one of its biggest inspirations. Between its top-down perspective, exploration, combat, and dungeon-like challenges, you'll probably catch some familiar vibes from the original Zelda and A Link to the Past along the way.

What I particularly love, though, is how Mina the Hollower manages to feel like a love letter to those classics without simply copying them. Its unique story and charming gothic aesthetic give it an identity of its own.

If one of the things that stayed with you after playing Ocarina of Time was its bittersweet take on growing up and letting go of the past, then Shadow of the Colossus is an excellent next stop.

This is a much quieter and more melancholic adventure, but it shares that ability to make you feel like you're part of something much bigger than yourself. Instead of exploring villages and dungeons, you'll travel across an enormous, almost deserted landscape on horseback, searching for sixteen colossal creatures. And each encounter is essentially a puzzle of its own, requiring you to figure out how to climb these mysterious beings and find their weak points before delivering the final blow.

Sources indicate that and trust me, there's something incredibly special about the atmosphere here! Much like Zelda, the world invites you to explore and take in its surroundings, but there's a sadness lingering beneath all that beauty. If you're looking for another adventure that makes you stop and think about the things we leave behind, this one is hard to beat.

Industry observers note that I mean, just look at Tunic’s cover! Do I need to say more? Jokes aside, this lovely indie adventure is another love letter to classic Zelda titles, and what I love most about it is how it perfectly understands the feeling of trusting players to let them figure things out for themselves.

It has been revealed that so if you loved the sense of discovery in Ocarina of Time, you're going to feel right at home here! Besides, you play as a little fox exploring a beautifully crafted world filled with hidden passages, dangerous enemies, challenging bosses, and secrets that often require a second look.

Industry observers note that also, Tunic makes exploration feel rewarding in a way that goes beyond simply finding another collectible. Even the game's instruction manual becomes part of the adventure, encouraging you to piece together its mysteries as you go! It's a lovely reminder of why discovering something on your own can be so much more exciting than having the game explain it to you.

If you're still craving that classic Zelda combination of dungeons, clever puzzles, memorable boss fights, and ingenious equipment, Death's Door deserves a spot on your list. It's another indie adventure with a strong love for the genre, but it manages to give those familiar ingredients a personality of its own.

According to recent reports, you play as a little crow working as a reaper, collecting souls in a strange world where death has become an increasingly complicated business. Along the way, you'll explore interconnected areas and face some genuinely challenging enemies. The combat is also fast and satisfying, while its dungeons offer plenty of clever environmental puzzles.

In a recent development, what really brings everything together, though, is the atmosphere. The world is wonderfully quirky, the soundtrack is fantastic, and there's a surprising amount of heart beneath its dark humor. It might not be Hyrule, but I think any Zelda fan looking for another compact adventure full of secrets and memorable encounters will have a great time here.

Sometimes, all you need after finishing a Zelda title is another gorgeous fantasy world to get lost in. And that's exactly what Kena: Bridge of Spirits offers. Its colorful environments and charming characters almost look like they've been pulled straight out of an animated movie, making it an easy recommendation if you loved the magical atmosphere of Ocarina of Time.

According to recent reports, but don't let the adorable presentation fool you, though. Kena's combat can get surprisingly challenging, especially when you face some of its larger bosses! Around here, you play as a spirit guide traveling through a beautiful but corrupted land, helping lost souls move on while uncovering the story behind the world around her.

According to recent reports, this means that exploration is a significant part of the experience, with environmental puzzles and little companions called Rot helping you interact with your surroundings. So there’s a little bit of everything, and it is quite easy to get lost in it!

Sure, most titles on this list are modern games because they're more accessible, but I remember that, back in the day, when I got the post-Ocarina of Time blues, it was Banjo-Tooie that saved me from the heartbreak.

Industry observers note that developed by Rare, this classic platformer takes the colorful gameplay of its predecessor (although you don't need to play the first game to enjoy this one) and expands it into a much bigger experience, with enormous interconnected worlds and plenty of secrets to uncover. There's just a lot to discover in each area, and the way different worlds connect makes exploration particularly rewarding.

Recent findings suggest that it's obviously a different kind of adventure from Zelda, leaning more heavily into 3D platforming, but there's something very familiar about the joy of exploring every corner of its environments. Plus, Banjo-Tooie has plenty of that same old-school magic.

One of the things I love most about Zelda is how its adventures can feel both fantastical and surprisingly emotional. If you're looking for another series that combines an imaginative world with a story about friendship, destiny, and growing up, Kingdom Hearts is definitely worth your time.

And the 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX collection is a great way to experience several important entries in the series and completely immerse yourself in this universe. Okay, maybe I'm cheating a little here, but we're in the middle of a new GTA era, so let me have this one!

It has been revealed that of course, I should also warn you that Kingdom Hearts has a much more confusing story than your average Zelda adventure. But underneath all those twists and mysterious characters is a genuinely heartfelt journey about the bonds we create and the people we want to protect.

Okay, hear me out: even though Metroid Prime Remastered is a first-person sci-fi adventure, it has more in common with Zelda than you might initially expect. In fact, its exploration structure is practically built around the same kind of progression that makes classic Zelda games so satisfying! If you loved finding a latest item in Ocarina of Time and immediately wondering which previously inaccessible areas you could now explore, you'll understand what I mean.

Playing as Samus Aran, you'll explore the interconnected regions of the planet Tallon IV, scanning your surroundings and uncovering the mysteries of an ancient civilization. As you acquire latest upgrades and abilities, paths that were previously blocked suddenly become accessible, encouraging you to revisit familiar locations with a fresh perspective.

The biggest difference is that you're doing all of this through a first-person perspective, with a much stronger emphasis on shooting and atmospheric exploration. But the satisfaction of gradually understanding how the world fits together is pure Zelda – a lovely reminder that a great adventure doesn't need to take place in Hyrule to capture that same magic.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You'd be forgiven for forgetting that Amy Hennig's superhero game Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra exists, but apparently it's still in development despite its many troubles and rumours to the contrary.
  • In a recent development, reassurance comes from Skydance's Slack work chat where, Kotaku notes, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told the team they'd spoken "directly" with Skydance leadership and could reassure staff the game wasn't going to be cancelled.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'd be forgiven for forgetting that Amy Hennig's superhero game Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra exists, but apparently it's still in development despite its many troubles and rumours to the contrary.

In a recent development, reassurance comes from Skydance's Slack work chat where, Kotaku notes, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told the team they'd spoken "directly" with Skydance leadership and could reassure staff the game wasn't going to be cancelled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly," Gigliotti reportedly told staff. "There is no truth to these claims.".

This follows a recent rumour that the action adventure title was potentially going to get the axe in the near future. The rumour originated from a Marvel 1943 fan account, and while the original X post has since been deleted, it didn't stop it from spreading online, including amongst the game's own development staff.

According to Kotaku's report, Rise of Hydra is close to its alpha state, despite seemingly five years of development. The game is stated to have had multiple issues through its long development.

Industry observers note that the current build is reportedly "light on gameplay", featuring only one interaction button. This is understood to be the result of Rise of Hydra having reportedly been originally envisioned as a Netflix game. According to the same report, the game is late and over budget, which resulted in cuts to its scope and scale throughout development.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was fully revealed in 2024, and is the debut title of Skydance New Media, the studio headed by veteran designer and writer Amy Hennig, who's famed for her work on the Uncharted series of games.

Though the game was originally planned for release in late 2025, it was later delayed to early 2026 and then again to "beyond early 2026". Earlier this summer, Paramount Games Studio boss Shawn Kittelsen said Rise of Hydra won't be out in 2026, but assured fans it remains in development. According to the report, Rise of Hydra was later delayed to 2027 and beyond.

Tensions are particularly high at the moment following the colossal recent Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, which has already resulted in some job losses at Paramount Games, a group that oversees the game's development, among other projects.

Recent findings suggest that whenever I mention that I write about mobile gaming, the inevitable first response from laymen and industry people alike is, 'Well, that's all just gacha, right?' And on the one hand, they're not necessarily right, but not wrong either. The random draw system is so pervasive that even many developers pit themselves against it, like with the upcoming Mixcity Swap.

Positioning itself as the anti-gacha, Mixcity Swap is an upcoming sports-themed card battler by Atypique Studio, releasing in 2027 for iOS and Android, that sees you taking on fast-paced, 10-minute matches. With only nine cards on the roster, the gameplay revolves around swapping in and out your athletes across different modes, doing so at the right interval as they activate their individual effects.

Industry observers note that in that way, I think positing it as anti gacha is a bit of a misnomer. At its core, Mixcity Swap looks to be an exciting standalone card game, and one that doesn't really need to pit itself against such a widely reviled mechanic to be successful.

But, I'll certainly be interested to see how Atypique plans to grow this game in future. We've got plenty of small-scale card battlers that avoid gacha, but a long-term live-service type release may be a very different beast to keep loyal to that ideal.

Sources indicate that still, if you find yourself wanting more card-battling action on mobile, then you're not without plenty of options to try. Just take a look at our list of the best card battlers on iOS, and you'll find some choice picks you can play right now!
